News.title: Tax rises ‘virtually inevitable’ after £8bn borrowing blow
News.content:
Tax rises are “virtually inevitable” after official figures showed the Treasury has borrowed £8bn more than expected so far this year.

Economists said the Chancellor faced an “uncomfortable” Budget after the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said spending outstripped tax receipts by £18.3bn in August, £3.5bn more than expected.

It means John Healey, the Chancellor, has borrowed £77.3bn so far this financial year, which is £8.1bn more than forecast.

Reacting to the figures, Emma Reynolds, the Chief Secretary to the Treasury, warned of “tough decisions” in Mr Healey’s Budget.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said: “The jump in borrowing in August compared to last year sets the stage for what is likely to be a much trickier Budget than Andy Burnham or Healey anticipated when they came to power.

“Another round of tax rises in October now looks inevitable.”

Philip Shaw, an economist at Investec, added: “We suspect that some tax increases are virtually inevitable.”

Ruth Gregory, deputy chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said the Chancellor would need to raise up to £14bn to restore the £24bn of fiscal headroom left by his predecessor Rachel Reeves to balance the books.

The Government’s debt interest bill soared to £8.8bn last month, according to the ONS, the biggest August figure since records began in 1997.

So far this year, the Treasury has spent £50bn on debt interest – £2bn more than forecast in March.

Nick Ridpath, an economist at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said: “Debt interest spending is a worryingly large share of overall government spending.

“Both higher borrowing costs and higher inflation make life harder for a Chancellor who is looking to bring down borrowing and to spend more on government priorities.”

Higher prices caused by the Iran war mean the Chancellor must pay more interest on the country’s huge stock of inflation-linked debt.

Inflation is also pushing up the welfare bill. The Government spent almost £30bn in August on benefits, 7pc more than a year ago.

Despite this, the Treasury continued to see substantial tax receipts. Income tax, capital gains, and National Insurance receipts stood at £231bn in the financial year to August.

That is £16.6bn higher than the same period a year ago.

Inheritance tax receipts also grew. They have risen to £3.8bn so far this financial year, a £100m increase compared with a year ago.

Ms Reynolds, the Treasury minister, said: “At a time when debt interest costs billions of pounds that could otherwise be spent on improving lives, we must always know where the money is coming from to pay for public services.

“That is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty.”

The figures also showed total debt rose to £2.985tn in August, taking the level just shy of £3tn.

Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, said: “Labour has lost control of the public finances.

“It takes a rare fiscal incontinence to have both the highest tax take in history and see borrowing still shoot up.”

News.title: France releases infertile Asian tiger mosquitoes to fight dengue threat
News.content:
French cities are fighting the growing threat of diseases like dengue, chikungunya and Zika in mainland Europe by releasing millions of sterile male Asian tiger mosquitoes.

Terratis, a new company in the southern city of Montpellier, is breeding infertile males on an industrial scale as a long-term solution to the rapid spread of the disease-carrying insects.

The sterile males are bred at a factory in the southern city of Montpellier and then released in urban hot zones where the mosquitoes are most prevalent. After they have mated, females reproduce only empty eggs for the remainder of their lives.

“By using this technique, the mosquitoes will have no descendants and then, in theory, we can reduce the population with each generation,” said Clelia Oliva, the founder of Terratis.

“We are confident of being able to achieve a reduction of between 70 and 90 per cent in the towns in which we are releasing the sterile mosquitoes.”

The company, which started only two years ago, has experienced a dramatic surge in demand in the last few years as France tries to deal with the invasive species.

News.title: ‘42 surgeries in 48 hours’: Doctors face extreme pressure in South Sudan
News.content:
Dr Mathiang Agany had no idea what was coming.

On a humid morning in April, scores of patients were rushed into his basic hospital in rural South Sudan after a shoot out between rival gangs. As the most senior doctor, Dr Agany, a maternal health specialist, had to perform 42 surgeries in just 48 hours.

Working alongside a second surgeon, a nurse and an anaesthetist, Dr Agany, 44, carefully extracted bullets from the vital organs of nine patients.

In 22 cases, he glued together fractured bones; and in four others he clamped damaged tissues shut and repaired torn organs.

Over the same 48 hour period, he also delivered seven babies through emergency c-sections.

“You are tired... but you can relax later,” he told The Telegraph over a video call.

“My job [was] to keep people alive”.

Separate to the ruinous four-year civil war in neighbouring Sudan, the violence plaguing South Sudan is inter-communal, a self-perpetuating cycle of cattle raiding, territorial disputes and revenge attacks carried out by armed youth militias from pastoral communities known as Titweng (“cattle guard”).

Young children were among the victims, including a four-year-old boy, whose leg was fractured by a gunshot, and a nine-month-old baby girl whose chest was grazed by the same bullet that killed her father.

News.title: Afghan medical students face expulsion from Pakistan
News.content:
An educational lifeline for young Afghan women banned by the Taliban from training as doctors in their homeland is in jeopardy after Pakistan’s medical authorities tried to have them expelled.

Several hundred Afghan female students studying across the border in Pakistan have been threatened with removal, amid rising tensions and tit-for-tat exchanges between the neighbours.

The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) which regulates medical education earlier this month ordered medical and dental colleges with Afghan students to kick them out.

Within days, major institutions including King Edward Medical University (KEMU), Shaikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Al Nahyan Medical and Dental College, and the Services Institute of Medical Sciences, had ordered Afghan students to leave.

The nationwide order was estimated to have affected around 1,000 Afghan students, with 35 per cent of those thought to be female students.

Provincial high courts have now temporarily halted the expulsion pending further hearings, but Afghan students told The Telegraph they were terrified their careers would be ended.

“The government’s decision aimed to send us to the Stone Age because the Taliban in Afghanistan have banned female education,” said Sabiha Daftani, one of the 22 Afghan students given orders on September 7 by KEMU in Lahore on to leave within 24 hours.

“The fear is constant and haunting us,” she said.

Sports.title: How Sir Alex Ferguson inadvertently set Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta on path to becoming Premier League ‘don’
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA is the “don” of the Premier League — and he looks here to stay.

The Arsenal boss has agreed terms on a new contract that will take his time in North London to ten years.



And it puts the Spaniard, 44, among a select group of Premier League managerial ‘Godfathers’ who have won the title and enjoyed long careers at their clubs.

Arsene Wenger was in charge of the Gunners for 22 years, while Sir Alex Ferguson did five more than that at Manchester United.



Pep Guardiola also managed a decade at Manchester City before he called it quits in the summer and Jurgen Klopp hit nine years with Liverpool.

Arteta is now set to follow in their footsteps and pundit Jamie Carragher argued this month how the Gunners boss now rules the roost in the Prem.



The former Liverpool defender, 48, explained: “He is the don at the moment. He is the Premier League champion.”

The power that Arteta wields at Arsenal — and within the English top flight — makes staying put an attractive option.

Carragher’s comments came after the Spaniard had a pop at the refereeing in the Gunners’ win at Sunderland this month.

Even though his side had won 2-0, Arteta made sure the decision to award the Black Cats a controversial penalty dominated the headlines.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

In Carragher’s eyes, it was Arteta “becoming the Sir Alex Ferguson of the Premier League right now” — and using the clout he carries after leading the Gunners to title glory.

Carragher added: “One of the journalists made a point about, no matter what question you asked him, he kept going back to the penalty.

“So he was determined to get the narrative out that this won’t happen again to his club. We’ve seen it with Sir Alex Ferguson — we’ve seen it with Jose Mourinho.”

In a strange way, it was actually Sir Alex that set Arteta on the path to becoming a Premier League don.

Arsenal swooped for the Spaniard from Everton on deadline day in the summer of 2011, days after they lost 8-2 to United.



Arteta was one of four signings made by the Gunners during a mad trolley dash and over the next five years he got to learn under Frenchman Wenger.

That was followed by three educational seasons as Guardiola’s assistant at City before he took the Emirates reins in December 2019.

Battles with Klopp naturally followed, with the pair famously squaring up to each either on the touchline at Anfield.

Arteta was viewed then as the plucky Prem newcomer looking to fight the elite.



Now having joined that class, he is hungry for more and this new contract is proof of that.

So is the way that Arsenal have strengthened their squad this summer. The signings were all very much of a ‘win-now’ nature.

None of this ‘bread today, jam tomorrow’ spin from Wenger’s days.

The champions’ two biggest arrivals this summer were Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa for a combined cost of £125million.

Both are 28 and proven in the Premier League. Clearly, Arteta has no desire to hang around and wants to strike while the iron is hot.



By signing a new contract, he will send that message to others — both inside and outside the club.

Arsenal want to tie down the likes of David Raya, Declan Rice and Jurrien Timber to fresh terms. That will be far easier now they know Arteta is staying.

The same goes for when the club pitches to potential new signings.

Arsenal still want a marquee forward and now whoever they target knows the manager is committed.



The question that remains, though, is how long for?

It is hard to see anyone replicating Sir Alex and Wenger’s stints in the modern era given the crazy schedule.

Guardiola and Klopp’s spells seem far more achievable and could work for Arteta.

Barcelona’s revamp of the Nou Camp will be done by then and manager Hansi Flick could have moved on, too.

A return to where Arteta began his career as a boy at Barca has always felt inevitable, or perhaps to Paris Saint-Germain.



It was at the French champions where the midfielder made his professional debut as an 18-year-old and he loved his time there.

But the concern for the fiercely ambitious Arteta must be that he will not find a club where he has the same power as Arsenal.

Guardiola discovered that and it is why he spent ten years at City — but only four at Barca.

Everything at the Emirates moves to Arteta’s beat and giving that up would not be easy.

After less than a year in charge, the Spaniard’s job title was changed from head coach to manager and he has never looked back.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Gunners have essentially been sculpted in his image — and he may not get the chance to do that again.

Arteta has also just joined the managerial royalty of the Premier League and does not look ready to give up that crown any time soon.

JOAO PEDRO has given a bizarre update on his playing future on LINKEDIN.

The Brazilian joined Chelsea from Brighton last summer in a £60million transfer.



Pedro, 24, penned a bumper new deal with the West Londoners in August which will keep him at Stamford Bridge until the summer of 2034.

And just a matter of weeks after tying his long-term future to the Blues, the striker has publicly reaffirmed his commitment to the club.



He wrote on his LinkedIn page: “Joining Chelsea Football Club was a huge moment for me, and looking back at everything that has happened since, I’m proud of how far we’ve come.

“I knew I was joining one of the biggest clubs in the world, with huge ambition and a special history.



“What I didn’t know was how quickly the club, the people here and life in London would become such an important part of my life.

“Since then, I’ve experienced some incredible moments in a Chelsea shirt.

“Winning the FIFA Club World Cup, having a season I’m proud of, being voted Player of the Season by our supporters and having the pride of becoming Chelsea’s number 9 are memories I’ll always carry with me.

“But this isn’t just about what we’ve already achieved.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“For me, making a decision like this comes down to more than what is happening in the moment.

“It’s about looking at where you are, what you still want to achieve and whether the environment around you is helping you get there.

“I think there is a lot to consider when deciding whether to stay or take on something new.



“Progress doesn’t always mean choosing something different. Sometimes it’s recognising when you’re surrounded by the right people, still learning, still being challenged and still excited by what you’re building together.

“I believe in where this club is going, I believe in the people around me and I want to be part of what comes next.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney says everyone close to JJ Gabriel knew exit was coming and opens up on what Man Utd prodigy is really like

WAYNE ROONEY insists everyone close to JJ Gabriel always “KNEW” he’d eventually want to leave Manchester United.

The 15-year-old whizzkid rocked Red Devils chiefs earlier this month by formally asking them to cancel his registration.



Gabriel’s agent has already put the teenager in the shop window, lining up talks with European giants Bayern Munich and Real Madrid.

The attacking midfielder’s imminent departure, which could end up costing United MILLIONS, has come as a shock to the Old Trafford brass, although Rooney – whose son Kai has come through the ranks with Gabriel – insists it’s always been on the cards.



Speaking on Disney+’s Stick to United, he said: “I’ve seen JJ grow up because he’s been in Kai’s team throughout the years, and I think that anyone close to it knew that was coming.

“In fairness to Manchester United, they’ve done everything, they’ve done absolutely everything to keep him, to keep him at the club.



“I think it’s been known that there’s been a desire to go and play probably in Spain, I think, I might be wrong, but this is what you’ve heard over the years.

“The club have treated him probably differently to the other players because he is such a special talent.

“I know, I recognise, I understand that because I was that player at Everton and I was getting that treatment at Everton which was you’re getting a bit more, your parents get given stuff, you’re getting that special treatment more than the other players are getting.

“Which, as a club, you need to do to try and keep your better players.

“It’s just disappointing, of course, because he is such a top player and he’s a lovely kid.

“So you never know whether it’s gone too far and whether there is a chance to stay.

“But I think everyone close to it has probably known that that was going to come.”

Having watched Gabriel up close on a number of occasions, Rooney firmly believes United will be missing out on a future top talent.



The club’s all-time leading goalscorer said of the youngster: “He is a top player.

“His ability, his balance, he has shown he can go up the ages and score goals.

“The next step is first-team football where it’s different, and you never know until you’re in there.

“But he’s such a special talent who understands the game really well.

“At some point this season he would [have] made his debut for the first-team, I’d imagine, so that’s where it’s disappointing.”



United boss Michael Carrick insists the club will handle Gabriel’s seemingly imminent departure with the utmost care.

MALANG SARR was reportedly ambushed and slapped after one of his representatives missed out on a massive payday following his switch to Saudi Arabia.

The former Chelsea centre-back was dining with two of his new NEOM team-mates in Malaga, Spain, in July.



L’equipe reported that “a group of imposing Frenchmen” interrupted the private dining room – reserved for the club – and dragged the star aside where a very loud conversation followed.

They ordered Sarr not to move, whilst the rest of the gathering also froze.



The star was said to be dragged away and repeatedly slapped in the assault – claims Sarr has refuted to French media.

The heated argument was said to revolve around his move to Saudi where the 27-year-old is set to earn £13million over the next three years.



Sarr’s deal expired on June 30 and he was permitted to join a new club on a free – despite his market value estimated to be around £17.2m.

And the player agreed to a new contract in just two days – without any agent involvement.

The day after signing, Sarr was pictured next to a NEOM-appointed agent holding a club shirt.

But with several agents being in-and-around the ace over the last few months, one in particular was said to be deeply cut by the quick deal – worsened by the fact he had had dealings with NEOM in the past.

Sports.content:

ANDROS TOWNSEND has revealed the unusual meals that he prepared to help recover from his freak accident with a pitch roller.

The former Tottenham and England winger, who now plays for PT Prachuap in Thailand, was run over by the machine while warming up at half-time.



Townsend, 35, thankfully came through the terrifying incident without serious injury, and was even able to come on as a substitute during the second half,.

But after the match, Townsend found his knee swelling and felt the need to aid his recovery with some specially prepared meals.



In an Instagram video the 13-cap star, who is no stranger to a quirky meal, said: “Over the next 24 hours, this is everything I ate to give my body what it needs to recover, support the inflammation process, and get me moving again without having to reach for medication.

“First up, six whole eggs. High-quality protein to support muscle repair.



“Then I started loading up on polyphenol-rich foods: blueberries, extra virgin olive oil, and raw cacao, which is packed with flavanols. These plant compounds have antioxidant and inflammation-reducing properties.

“Next, smoked salmon, packed with omega-3s, which are involved in inflammatory signalling and supporting muscle recovery.



“Raw cheese gives me calcium to support bone health. And then an orange gives me vitamin C, essential for making collagen.”

Far from being done, Townsend then revealed his painstakingly prepared second meal.

“Wild-caught salmon again with tomatoes,” he began. “Tomatoes give me more powerful antioxidants as well as vitamin C.

“And then one of my favourites for this situation: chicken feet slow-cooked for eight hours in a soup.

“This gives me collagen from the meat and gelatin from the liquid, rich in amino acids like glycine and proline, the building blocks associated with collagen-rich tissues like tendons, ligaments, and cartilage.



“And I paired that with kiwi for another big hit of vitamin C”.

Townsend finished his video by vowing: “Food is medicine.”

The shocking roller incident immediately went viral, with Townsend subsequently appearing on Piers Morgan Uncensored to explain what actually happened.

He said: “I didn’t see it coming. It was at half-time, we were going out to warm up. I saw two rollers on either side of the pitch.

“I remember thinking to myself, ‘I’ve never seen that before in my career, what are they doing?’



“But we got called to warm up. Didn’t think anything of it. The next I saw him was when I was literally underneath him and thankfully no serious damage.

“A couple of bumps and bruises but managed to walk away unscathed, luckily. Every time I see it, I’m cringing, I’m in disbelief. When I sent it to my kids, my kids thought it was AI.

“Literally, I had to explain to them, for the next ten minutes, that it was real. It’s horrible to watch back and to see what could have been.

“Thankfully, I was fortunate I did manage to fall on to the floor at the right time, so nothing snapped as the roller went over me. And I’m here today to laugh about and tell the story.”

Sports.title: Why Man Utd fans do not need to panic as shock stat shows they should actually be FOURTH in Premier League
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED have had a mixed start to the Premier League season and are sitting in a disappointing 12th in the table.

The Red Devils have only won once in their opening five fixtures with two losses and two draws.



Matheus Cunha was on hand with a deflected strike to salvage a point against Fulham at the weekend.

The below-par results have seen pressure start to mount on club legend and manager Michael Carrick.



However, Opta stats have revealed that the club are performing much better than their bottom-half placement would suggest in terms of expected points.

The analysis platform suggests that the club should expect to be FOURTH in the table with the quality of their performances.



This raises hopes for fans that United can turn around their fortunes and shoot up the table after the international break.

Speaking after the draw at Craven Cottage, Carrick explained points in recent matches which had gone against his side.

He said: “It’s not been ideal. It was always going to come at some point.

“We’re looking at it and think, Everton, a 25-yard shot into the top corner, the Man City goal is not a goal and, today, we see that own goal.

“One of those things, but they are pretty fine margins. They are things that have flipped it.

“I know we can do better, we need to do better at certain things but at the same time I’m not despondent because we have shown some good signs as well.”

United are not the only team who should expect to be higher in the Prem table.



Basement boys Tottenham should actually be 13th in the league according to Opta’s analysis of their performances but find themselves bottom on goal difference.

The North London outfit scored their first league goals of the season in the 3-2 defeat to Aston Villa on Sunday.

But the lack of final product before then has seen Roberto De Zerbi‘s side collect just two points.

Sports.title: Fuming Marco Silva hints he will QUIT Benfica just months after leaving Fulham for Portuguese giants
Sports.content:
Next

MARCO SILVA has hinted that he could leave Benfica… just three months after taking the job.

The Portuguese boss, 49, left Fulham over the summer after five years in charge at Craven Cottage.



Silva went on to replace Real Madrid-bound Jose Mourinho at Benfica, but isn’t wholly enjoying the experience so far.

Last weekend’s 3-1 defeat at Porto left the Lisbon side already trailing their opponents by five points at the top of the table.



Benfica’s task had been made infinitely more difficult when former Tottenham and Barcelona centre-back Clement Lenglet was sent off after just 35 minutes.

Lenglet’s red card was for the lightest of slaps to the back of Andre Silva‘s head, the striker then theatrically going down and rolling around.



Speaking after his side’s 3-1 defeat, the Benfica boss suggested that officials in Portugal can be “influenced” by pre-match comments.

Per Portuguese outlet Record, Silva said: “I won’t comment on the sending off.

“If the club has something to say about the match, I think it should say it.

“I don’t know if I’ll be able to continue like this until the end of the season, because I come from a different culture.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“Here, unfortunately, you can influence referees before matches, after them and during the week, and sometimes it works. I’m not going to go down that route.”

Porto president Andre Villas-Boas, formerly manager of Chelsea and Tottenham, hit back at Silva’s comments.

Villas-Boas called some of the decisions against his own team “difficult to understand” – but labelled Lenglet’s red card as “great refereeing”.



He also added: “The statistic I know is that Porto have 21 points and seven wins.”

Silva had his fair share of run-ins with officials during his stint in England.

As recently as April he was fined £90,000 and issued with a one-match touchline ban for criticising referee John Brooks following a 1-0 defeat at West Ham.

Silva’s Fulham successor Alvaro Arbeloa is yet to win a Premier League in charge – and has spoken out about the officials himself after their latest draw.

The West Londoners were denied a triumph over Manchester United by a late Matheus Cunha equaliser last Sunday.

Sports.title: What Mikel Arteta’s rivals think about Arsenal boss as new contract 'agreed'
Sports.content:
What Mikel Arteta’s rivals think about Arsenal boss as new contract 'agreed'

Mikel Arteta is close to signing a new contract at Arsenal with the Gunners having rewarded the Spaniard for his work at the Emirates Stadium following his appointment in 2019

View 4 Images Mikel Arteta has agreed a new deal with Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta has agreed a new deal with Arsenal in a move that will be welcomed by the Gunners - but not their rivals. The Spanish coach was appointed in 2019 as a replacement for Unai Emery and has done some brilliant work with the north London side.

‌



He has completely reversed the club’s fortunes over recent years to take them from mid-table to the Premier League title. Arteta has also restored Arsenal at the top of the European game, having led them to the Champions League final last term.

‌



With Arteta now set to remain with the club for the foreseeable future, his rivals will now have to continue mulling over their attempts to get the better of him.

‌



But what have they already said? Mirror Football takes a trawl through some past interviews and press conferences to find out exactly what they think of the Arsenal boss.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Xabi Alonso

Let’s start with someone who knows Arteta very well: Xabi Alonso. The two Spaniards are childhood friends and have embarked on very similar careers, with glittering playing stints in the Premier League, while they have now turned to management.

They have already locked horns this season, with the Gunners running out 2-1 winners in the Premier League earlier this month.

Speaking ahead of that game, Alonso praised his friend for his work at the Emirates and vowed that they would never think differently of each other despite now being direct rivals.

‌



He said: “No, it [their relationship] won't change. Our friendship and mutual respect won't change because of competition, because the system he's built at Arsenal is truly remarkable, and it's a long-term process.”

Andoni Iraola

Alonso is not the only close friend that Arteta has in the Premier League. Current Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola also grew up alongside the pair in the Basque region of Spain.

And he has already played quite a crucial role in his career so far, with his former side Bournemouth having held Manchester City last season to hand the Gunners the title.

‌



Iraola claimed that it was just the reward that both Arteta and Arsenal deserved after a number of near misses.

Speaking at the time, he said: “Happy for him because I think he has done an incredible job there. For a lot of seasons very consistent. Sometimes he has been so close, the reward has probably come in the right moment."

View 4 Images Arteta and Alonso are childhood friends (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Michael Carrick

Another top-flight manager who is well-acquainted with Arteta is Manchester United boss Michael Carrick. The pair faced off on a number of occasions during their playing careers and have already sparred on the touchline.

They at first clashed back in the 2021/22 season, with Carrick overseeing an interim role at United. He was successful on that occasion with a 3-2 win and repeated that result last term.

Regardless, Carrick remains a big fan of Arteta and the work he has done in north London. He said: ''I think he's done a very good job at Arsenal and you can see they're going in a certain direction and been pretty strong with that.

‌



''He was a terrific player, very technical, and that’s the way his teams plays and obviously the way he has coached them in that style shows what type of player he was.''

View 4 Images Carrick is a big fan of Arteta's work at Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Unai Emery

Arteta’s longevity at the Emirates Stadium is a huge departure from his predecessor Unai Emery. The Spaniard was afforded just 18 months in north London after replacing Arsene Wenger.

‌



And that decision looks to have been for the betterment of both Arsenal and Emery - the pair having thrived apart.

The now Aston Villa coach has praised his compatriot for steering the ship back on course. He said: “The work Arteta is doing there now is brilliant and he’s doing more or less everything I was thinking needed to be done there.”

There was a brief flashpoint between the two when Emery chose not to shake Arteta’s hand after a game but that does not appear to have caused a lasting issue since then.

‌



View 4 Images Arteta and Maresca have already clashed this season (Image: Getty Images)

Enzo Maresca

One of Arteta’s main rivals this season looks to be Enzo Maresca. The Italian has replaced both his and Arteta’s former tutor Pep Guardiola at the Etihad and will be expected to put together a title charge throughout the season.

Speaking about the pair’s learnings under Guardiola, Maresca said: “Probably we [himself and Arteta] both have to be thankful because we worked besides and next to the one that I consider the best manager in the world. Probably we both have been quite lucky to work with Pep."

‌



Roberto De Zerbi

While Maresca will be one of those plotting Arteta’s downfall, the same could certainly be said of Roberto De Zerbi. The Italian is now in charge of Arsenal’s North London rivals Tottenham.

And while some fans might be wanting some hostility between the two, De Zerbi made his admiration of Arteta clear during his spell with former club Brighton.

He said: “Arteta is a great manager. He is very young and his style is clear. I enjoy watching Arsenal games… I try to learn something when I watch them. He was lucky to work with Pep Guardiola and now I think Arteta is one of the best coaches in the world.”

Sports.title: Liverpool close in on Richard Hughes successor with FSG sporting director decision close
Sports.content:
Liverpool close in on Richard Hughes successor with FSG sporting director decision close

Liverpool's majority owners, Fenway Sports Group (FSG), have been pondering who to replace Richard Hughes with following his departure as sporting director earlier this month

View 2 Images Julian Ward is expected to become Liverpool's new sporting director (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Fenway Sports Group have reportedly decided to make an internal appointment to replace Richard Hughes as Liverpool's sporting director.

‌



Hughes left his role earlier this month following a turbulent summer, choosing to join Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal. The former Bournemouth chief spent two years in the hot seat at Anfield, overseeing the big-money transfers of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola.

‌



His departure followed that of Michael Edwards, who stepped down as the chief executive officer of football of FSG in July. A busy summer also saw a consortium, which includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, take over a third of the club.

‌



FSG have scoured the market for Hughes' replacement before deciding to keep things in-house by choosing Julian Ward. The Athletic reports that Ward will switch from FSG technical director to Liverpool's sporting director, with a process overseen by FSG president Mike Gordon now nearing its conclusion.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Ward has been at the club since 2012 and has held a variety of roles at Liverpool and owners FSG. He was European scouting manager for Spain and Portugal, then loan pathways manager and then assistant sporting director.

Ward was promoted to become sporting director following the departure of Edwards in the summer of 2022, but stepped down at the end of the 2022/23 season, shocking Liverpool in the process. He returned to the fold by following Edwards to FSG in 2024, where he has been tasked with overseeing player development pathways and the academy, and is now returning to Anfield as sporting director.

During his short-lived previous spell as sporting director, Ward oversaw the signings of Luis Diaz, Darwin Nunez and Cody Gakpo, among other players. He was also behind the arrival of Alexis Mac Allister in the summer of 2023, having stayed longer than his exit date to seal the deal for the Brighton midfielder.

‌



View 2 Images Julian Ward (second left), with Michael Edwards (centre) and Richard Hughes (second right) (Image: Nikki Dyer - LFC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

It means that David Woodfine will remain as Liverpool's assistant sporting director, working underneath Ward, while Pedro Marques - who was another candidate for the role and a close colleague of Ward - will stay as FSG's director of football development.

FSG did speak to external candidates, including Brentford technical director Lee Dykes, before deciding to elevate Ward back into the hot seat. He will therefore take charge of player recruitment at Liverpool following a difficult summer.

Article continues below

Hughes' spell in charge was bookended by the £123million signing of Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, while Victor Munoz, Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo all also arrived this summer. But the slow-burn nature of the summer transfer window raised plenty of eyebrows and caused some friction, with Mark Burchill and Craig McKee also leaving the club to follow Hughes to Saudi Arabia.

Andoni Iraola, who arrived following an impressive spell at Bournemouth to replace Arne Slot, was exasperated by the club's transfer business, which saw a net spend of £172m accumulated.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney makes Man Utd transfer claim on JJ Gabriel's next club decision
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney makes Man Utd transfer claim on JJ Gabriel's next club decision

There is a lot of talk over where JJ Gabriel's future could lie after he asked to leave Manchester United

View Image JJ Gabriel has told Manchester United of his desire to leave the club. (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

Manchester United legend Wayne Rooney has claimed that a move to Spain could be on the cards for JJ Gabriel, with the youngster's exit from the club an open secret to those close to the situation. The 15-year-old has told the club that he wishes to leave.

‌



Talks have been held with Barcelona and Real Madrid over a potential move, although United could block the exit, with a tribunal then needed to sort the situation. Gabriel was expected to be part of the squad and potentially make his first-team debut for United in the Carabao Cup clash vs Brighton before the news broke.

‌



Rooney made the breakthrough as a teenager at Everton, with his son, Kai, also now playing in the United academy set-up. The former striker has suggested that a move to Spain could be the most likely option, despite the club doing everything possible to try and convince him to stay.

‌



Lewis Hall says it was a 'no-brainer' to snub Man Utd despite transfer interest READ MORE :

Speaking on Disney+'s Stick to United, Rooney said: "I think that anyone close to it knew that was coming. In fairness to Manchester United, they've done everything, they've done absolutely everything to keep him, to keep him at the club.

"I think it's been known that there's been a desire to go and play probably in Spain, I think, I might be wrong, but this is what you've heard over the years. The club have treated him probably differently to the other players because he is such a special talent.

"I know, I recognise, I understand that because I was that player at Everton and I was getting that treatment at Everton which was you're getting a bit more, your parents get given stuff, you're getting that special treatment more than the other players are getting. Which as a club you need to do to try and keep your better players.

‌



"It's just disappointing, of course, because he is such a top player and he's a lovely kid. So you never know whether it's gone too far and whether there is a chance to stay.

"But I think everyone close to it has probably known that that was going to come".

‌



Gabriel ranks among the brightest prospects in the United youth set-up. Despite his tender age of 15, he has netted 29 times and registered four assists across 32 outings for the club's Under-18s side.

He has also bagged two goals and laid on two assists in two matches for the Under-21s.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Article continues below

Addressing the matter, United manager Michael Carrick is determined to shield the youngster from undue pressure. "He's a young boy, JJ, and I think it's important that we certainly don't play anything out here," he said.

"I think the exposure and the scrutiny and everything, you've got to be careful and be sensible and think of him as much as anything. So the situation will work itself out, whatever way it's going to work itself out. Making sure he's okay is the important thing."

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho given fresh escape route after nightmare Aston Villa start
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho given fresh escape route after nightmare Aston Villa start

Former Manchester United star Alejandro Garnacho only joined Aston Villa from Chelsea in the summer but the forward could potentially be on the move once again, with clubs already eyeing him

View 2 Images Garnacho joined Aston Villa from Chelsea in the summer (Image: Getty Images)

Alejandro Garnacho is reportedly being monitored by Spanish clubs after a difficult start to life with Aston Villa. The former Manchester United man only joined the Midlands side on a season-long loan deal in the summer from Chelsea.

‌



But Garnacho, 22, has been limited to just 31 minutes of action so far this season, and has not even come off the bench in any of Villa’s last three games.

‌



His switch to Villa Park will become permanent for a fee of around £43million should certain conditions be met. But that already appears unlikely.

‌



According to Mail Online, clubs in La Liga are watching Garnacho’s situation. The forward was actually born in Madrid and had a spell with Atletico Madrid’s academy before his switch to Manchester United.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Asked recently what Garnacho needs to do to earn an opportunity with the club, Villa boss Unai Emery said: “Continue working. Work, work, train, work.

“When he can have minutes to play, try to play well. He is progressing, but we have players in front of him now. George Hemmings is playing fantastic. Alysson is also understanding things well and is giving us things I want. [Ibrahim] Mbaye also responded well.

“We want a competitive team and players to compete in the style we have. Garnacho is a little bit behind because of some circumstances we had in pre-season. It is time to be patient for the time he needs.”

‌



View 2 Images Garnacho has played just 31 minutes for Aston Villa this season (Image: Getty Images)

Having been left out of the latest Argentina squad, he will now join Villa on a mid-season training camp in Spain, where he will certainly hope to catch Emery’s eye.

Garnacho’s career has taken a sharp downturn over recent seasons. After scoring 26 goals in 144 appearances for Manchester United, he left the club in a £40m move to Premier League rivals Chelsea last summer.

Article continues below

He netted eight goals in 43 appearances for Chelsea across his debut campaign but just one of those came in the Premier League. New boss Xabi Alonso made it clear that he had little future at Stamford Bridge ahead of his move to Villa. Garnacho has just under six years remaining on his current contract at Stamford Bridge.

Villa have a just under three-week wait for their next Premier League game which is set to come against Brentford on October 10. They will then take on Fenerbahce in their first Champions League home game of the campaign.

Sports.title: Andrew Robertson ‘feels sorry’ for Trent Alexander-Arnold amid Real Madrid issues
Sports.content:
Andrew Robertson ‘feels sorry’ for Trent Alexander-Arnold amid Real Madrid issues

Former Liverpool star Trent Alexander-Arnold has endured a tricky time since joining Real Madrid last summer and his former teammate Andrew Robertson has now spoken out

View 2 Images Andrew Robertson has leapt to Trent Alexander-Arnold's defence (Image: Getty Images)

Ex-Liverpool star Andrew Robertson has admitted he feels sorry for former teammate Trent Alexander-Arnold due to the increased level of criticism he receives. The pair struck up a brilliant partnership during their respective spells at Anfield.

‌



They were key to Liverpool claiming two Premier League titles under Jurgen Klopp and Arne Slot, while they also played a role in the club’s Champions League success. Despite their glittering spell at Anfield, Alexander-Arnold faced severe criticism for defensive errors, while he has never quite managed to establish himself in the England side.

‌



And Robertson says he sympathised with his former teammate. Speaking on The Overlap, the Scottish defender said: "It's very different when you are English, compared to another nationality.

‌



“I always said to Trent, 'I will never get as much high praise as you, but I'll never get as much criticism as you.'"

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He added: "The way I defended at Liverpool compared to Trent was very different. I had Sadio helping me out and he was a bit more aggressive so if I missed [a tackle], he'd usually be there.

“With Mo [Salah], we didn't want him coming back towards our box. A lot of times, Trent was waiting on someone like [Jordan Henderson] to come over, so, sometimes, I started to feel sorry for him."

Alexander-Arnold has since departed Liverpool, having joined Spanish giants Real Madrid on a free transfer last summer. He has endured an inconsistent spell in La Liga so far, having started just 14 league games during his debut campaign.

‌



View 2 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold has not hit the heights expected of him at Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

That has continued this season, with new manager Jose Mourinho preferring Denzel Dumfries at right-back. But Robertson remains sure that Alexander-Arnold has the talent to be a success at the Bernabeu.

"I've seen him lock out [Kylian] Mbappe at PSG. In the Champions League finals, he was unbelievable," he said. "Trent is a very, very good defender… [in his] best games, he was an unbelievable one-v-one defender.

Article continues below

"Now, at times, he maybe makes mistakes. But we all do. But it's if [Trent] had this stigma around him, that he can't defend. And he's had that from a very early age. It's as if he can't shift it."

Like Alexander-Arnold, Robertson left Liverpool this summer as he joined Premier League rivals Tottenham. The 32-year-old has started all but one of his new club’s league games this season, with Roberto De Zerbi’s men currently without a win and bottom of the table.

Sports.title: Lewis Hall says it was a 'no-brainer' to snub Man Utd despite transfer interest
Sports.content:
Lewis Hall says it was a 'no-brainer' to snub Man Utd despite transfer interest

Lewis Hall has chosen to extend his contract with Newcastle despite being heavily linked with Manchester United in the summer, explaining the reasons for his decision

View 2 Images Lewis Hall has chosen to extend his Newcastle contract (Image: Serena Taylor, Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Lewis Hall admits it was a "no-brainer" to sign an extension with Newcastle despite Manchester United's interest as he talked up the impact of Matthias Jaissle.

‌



The new boss, who replaced Eddie Howe in the summer, has made an immediate impression and impressed with a Magpies side that endured a poor campaign last time out and looked to have lost a bit of direction under the previous regime.

‌



Hall had to watch leading lights like Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon leave St James' Park in the summer, which led to speculation he would follow. United were particularly keen and need a left-back at Old Trafford, but Newcastle dug their heels in and maintained he wouldn't be sold.

‌



Hall has got his head down under Jaissle, still only 38, and quickly decided that the former Red Bull Salzburg manager can lead Newcastle to great heights, committing to the club for the next five years.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Quizzed on whether the transfer talk impacted on him he said: “No, honestly, it didn’t [affect me]. I guess whenever you’re linked to another team, you know that you’re doing something right. I guess it’s just a credit to your own performances and how you are as a player, how you are as a person.

“I took that as a positive, but at the same time, I knew how much I love playing here and I knew that since the manager came in, I knew the ambitions and what we wanted to achieve.

“After not many conversations, not many training sessions, I knew that the manager was going to be really good for this club and I knew that as a team, bringing in new players and improving the squad was really important and as soon as we did that, it was a no-brainer really to sign.”

‌



View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle has made an immediate impression in Newcastle

Newcastle have won two of their five games, losing just the once, with Jaissle impressing as he transitions in a host of new summer signings, many of whom were largely unknown quantities.

Hall, whilst enduring difficult moments, which included giving away a stoppage time penalty against Liverpool, has been a strong performer and that has seen him recalled to the England squad.

Article continues below

He missed out on the World Cup in the summer, which owed to his performance levels dipping in the final weeks of the season. Hall was left frustrated that Howe played him on the right, not his natural position, which he reportedly attributed to his form dropping off.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel 'reaches first major agreement' as Man Utd star tells four clubs his preference
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel 'reaches first major agreement' as Man Utd star tells four clubs his preference

Manchester United starlet JJ Gabriel expressed a desire to leave Old Trafford last week and has since been linked with some of the biggest clubs in the world

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel of Manchester United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel reportedly wants to move to Spain if he is granted an exit from the Red Devils. It emerged earlier this month that Gabriel had expressed a desire to leave United, and there are already reports of where the playmaker could end up joining.

‌



Reports last week claimed that Gabriel had refused to take part in training for United ahead of their Carabao Cup third-round tie against Brighton. The 15-year-old was expected to be involved in the matchday squad for Michael Carrick’s side before expressing a desire to leave United.

‌



Gabriel has been tipped to have a bright future in the game, and would have been United’s youngest-ever player had he made his debut against the Seagulls at Old Trafford last week. Yet Gabriel's determination to leave United has sparked intense speculation surrounding the youngster's next move.

‌



A new update has surfaced from Spain suggesting that Gabriel could be heading across Europe should he leave United. Spanish publication Sport have reported that Gabriel's shortlist of potential destinations now features four clubs, two of which are based in Spain. Real Madrid and Barcelona are among those reportedly keen on securing Gabriel's signature, alongside Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



The report further claims that Gabriel and his camp have already visited Spain, touring both Madrid and Barcelona. The United starlet has reportedly reached a 'first major agreement' to join one of those clubs instead of any other team. Reports suggest Gabriel is now keen on a move to Spain, giving Barcelona and Real Madrid the upper hand in the race to sign the coveted United youngster.

Gabriel has enjoyed an impressive opening few weeks of the season, most recently scoring a hat-trick against Sabah in the UEFA Youth League earlier this month. The playmaker has also contributed two goals and two assists across just two appearances for United's Under-21s in Premier League 2.

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel of Manchester United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Despite his request to depart, Gabriel remains registered with United for the remainder of the season and cannot be de-registered. United believe the matter can still be resolved, despite Gabriel's unexpected desire to leave the club. The teenager is just a couple of weeks away from being eligible to sign a scholarship with United when he turns 16 on October 6, and will need to wait until his 17th birthday before putting pen to paper on a professional contract.

Speaking on Friday, Carrick was keen to shift the focus away from speculation surrounding the teenager and towards his wellbeing. He said: "I’ll just repeat what I said [earlier this week]: he’s a young boy, it’s important we don’t put anything out here, the exposure and scrutiny we have to be careful.

"We have to be sensible and think about him. The situation will work itself out."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta 'receives bumper pay rise' as Arsenal boss reaches new contract agreement
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta 'receives bumper pay rise' as Arsenal boss reaches new contract agreement

After a hugely successful year last season, Mikel Arteta has decided to extend his stay at the Emirates Stadium by agreeing to sign a new Arsenal deal

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta is set to remain at Arsenal for the long-term (Image: Getty)

Mikel Arteta has reportedly reached an agreement with Arsenal to sign a bumper new contract at the Emirates Stadium. His current deal in north London expires at the end of the current season.

‌



However, fresh terms between the Gunners manager and the club have been agreed, and he is set to sign a new deal, according to the BBC. Moreover, his new terms are set to include a sizeable pay rise from his current £10million-per-year deal, which includes an additional £5m in bonuses.

‌



It's unclear as to how long the contract will be, but it's believed it will take Arteta, who was appointed as manager in 2019, into his tenth year of service.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Last week, Arteta was asked about contract talks with the club. He replied: "They [the fans] don't have to worry about any of that because I want to be here. I'm extremely happy and I feel very grateful to work with the people I work with."

Arsenal co-chairman Josh Kroenke also made it clear at the start of June that the club would do everything they could to ensure Arteta remained in north London.

‌



Shortly after the Gunners won the Premier League, the American said: "Keeping Mikel around is [an] utmost priority. I think the good news for Arsenal fans worldwide is he's enjoying the project.

View 3 Images Kroenke stated keeping Arteta was of vital importance to the north Londoners (Image: Stuart MacFarlane, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

"He's enjoying being here and from his time as a player all the way up until now, he's an Arsenal man through and through."

‌



He also added: "If there is a singular person you can trace this all back to, I'm going to give 100% credit to Mikel, his staff and the players.

"Those are the ones. As much as Mikel is putting together our tactics, the players have got to go play the games, they've got to go and win for you."

View 3 Images Arsenal suffered their first defeat of the season (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

Last year, Arsenal ended their barren 22-year run without a league title and were a penalty shootout away from winning the Champions League. They also got to the final of the League Cup, only to lose 2-0 to Manchester City at Wembley Stadium.

The north Londoners have started the new campaign well, winning all but one of their matches in all competitions. Their winning start was ended last weekend by Brighton and Hove Albion, who secured a shock 3-0 victory on the South Coast.

Sports.title: Giants' star quarterback Dart could be forced to undergo knee surgery
Sports.content:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart could be forced to undergo knee surgery that would end his season, according to ESPN.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Dart's injured left knee is being evaluated in the aftermath of the starting quarterback exiting the game in defeat at the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night.

Dart was hurt less than four minutes into the game while being pressured on third-and-eight.

Rams linebacker Byron Young hit Dart from the quarterback's right side, sending him into linebacker Josaiah Stewart, who undercut Dart's legs, resulting in a heavy fall.

Sports.title: Leigh and Wigan conduct to be investigated by RFL
Sports.content:
Leigh Leopards and Wigan Warriors will be subject to an independent investigation into their conduct and actions over the past 12 months, the Rugby Football League (RFL) has said.

The Leopards and the Warriors have had an ongoing dispute for almost 12 months, dating back to the high-profile ticketing saga that led to Leigh's owner Derek Beaumont saying his club would not participate in the fixture over a disagreement about their ticket allocation of 4,800.

They ultimately did play the game and were eliminated from the play-offs with Wigan winning 18-6.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League semi-final match between Wakefield Trinity and Leigh Leopards

With the Warriors set to host Wakefield in the play-off semi-final on Saturday, matters reignited again over the weekend after an original post from Wigan detailed ticketing arrangements for whichever side visited the Brick this weekend in the play-offs would receive an allocation of 5,000 tickets for safety reasons.

Leigh were beaten by Wakefield Trinity in their eliminator match, where a win for the Leopards would have seen them progress to face Wigan instead.

Beaumont put himself in the spotlight again with a tirade on social media site X following Wigan's statement and his activity could also breach the RFL's own social media code of conduct.

The RFL said in a statement: "The independent Rugby Football League and RL Commercial Boards have issued a letter to both Leigh Leopards RLFC and Wigan Warriors RLFC advising them there will be an independent investigation into the conduct and actions of both clubs and the governing body in relation to matters extending over the last 12 months.

"The RFL and RL Commercial will not make any further comment until the investigation is complete."

Wigan finished top of the Super League regular season table, while Leigh finished fifth.

Sports.title: Menzies reveals heart attack scare before Matchplay incident
Sports.content:
Players Championship 29 winner Cameron Menzies has revealed he feared he was suffering a heart attack on a flight to Switzerland, prompting him to take a serious look at his lifestyle.

Menzies saw off Gian van Veen 8-4 in the final to claim his second ProTour title of 2026 on Tuesday.

Menzies continued his sparkling Players Championship form to claim a fourth PDC ranking title at Maassport Den Bosch, after an impressive string of seven straight wins.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cameron Menzies withdrew from the World Matchplay of Darts after becoming unwell during his second-round match against Ross Smith

After capturing his second title of the year, the Scot, reflected on his medical episode in Blackpool when he was forced to withdraw from the tournament after being taken ill during his second-round match against Ross Smith.

"Even before [the incident] happened, as you can see I've lost a bit of weight. Last year I was heading to Switzerland and I genuinely thought I was having a heart attack on the plane," explained Menzies. "I went for scans because heart problems is something that runs in my family.

"They told me I needed to lose weight, but the thing with the Ross Smith match is that I went for tests after and they believe it was dehydration but it caused my blood pressure to go high because I was panicking. I've never had that before."

Menzies: We're not all athletes here!

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first-round clash between Luke Humphries and Menzies at the World Matchplay

The 37-year-old World Cup semi-finalist continued: "I went for blood tests to check for more serious issues, including my heart. I spent 10 hours in Glasgow Jubilee Hospital, but everything came back fine apart from my blood pressure being a little high. They believe what happened in Blackpool was dehydration, so I just need to look after myself a bit more.

"I'll go and have some water and electrolytes after this, but we're not all athletes here, I get that! It's long days. I've been here since 9.30 this morning. These are long days, so you have to look after yourself. I'm getting older now, so I need to look after myself.

"My breakfast today was porridge, so I've not eaten all day. I would usually go and get a pizza, but I need to try to be better.

"A lot of players go jogging or walking now. Darts is probably better than it's ever been because all these young kids are coming through and they're all fit athletes. It's not like when we grew up playing in clubs and pubs. These guys are in youth systems. They're catching up."

Menzies averaged more than 101 in his opening victory over Nick Kenny before surviving an impressive comeback from Canada's Jim Long in a last-leg decider.

After seeing off Slovenia's Benjamin Pratnemer 6-4, he then defeated top seed Wessel Nijman by the same scoreline.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Scotland's 8-5 win over Republic of Ireland in the quarter-finals from the World Cup of Darts in Frankfurt

Menzies saw off Jeffrey de Graaf 6-3 with another stellar average to reach the semi-finals, where he defeated Kevin Doets to book his place in a third Players Championship final in his last five events.

He stormed into a 5-0 lead, denying Van Veen a dart at double during a brilliant opening burst, before the Dutchman responded with three consecutive legs.

The Scot held his nerve, however, winning three of the next four legs to seal victory and claim the £15,000 top prize in the Netherlands.

"I'm grateful to be in this position and it's not like I take it for granted or anything, but I would like to finish the year on a high. I'm in the Worlds and maybe the Grand Slam, so I'm in a very fortunate position," said Menzies.

Sports.title: Arteta agrees new Arsenal contract
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has agreed a new deal to extend his stay at Arsenal.

The 44-year-old's existing contract with the Premier League champions, signed in September 2024, was due to expire next summer.

But the Spaniard, who was appointed in 2019, has committed his future to the club and confirmation of his new agreement is expected during this international break.

When asked about his contract situation ahead of Arsenal's trip to Brighton on Saturday, Arteta said: "I think we are all very much aligned; whenever the time is right, we'll get that done. There is nothing to be concerned about.

"I think we both have the same ambition and the same will. So whenever we have time, we'll get that resolved."

Arteta has transformed Arsenal's fortunes during his tenure and guided the club to their first Premier League title in 22 years last season following three straight second-place finishes.

He also led the Gunners to only their second Champions League final, which they lost on penalties to Paris Saint-Germain. He has previously won an FA Cup and three Community Shields.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta says he and the club are very much aligned when it comes to signing a new contract with the club.

'Arteta's new deal agreed but not signed'

Analysis by Sky Sports News' Gary Cotterill:

"It's not signed yet. Officially, the club are not saying it has been agreed, but our understanding is that an agreement has been in place for a couple of weeks.

"Mikel Arteta alluded to that on Friday when I asked him about it. He said they are aligned and in agreement.

"So, I believe the deal is agreed. It's now a case of sorting the formalities, sitting down and signing the contract.

"I expect that to happen during the next international break, potentially within the next two weeks.

"When he signed his current contract two years ago, that was also completed during the international break, on September 12.

"He tends to compartmentalise things. He has a break, then turns his attention to his future.

"The agreement has been in place for weeks. The only thing left now is to get the contract signed and make the announcement. The full details of the deal should follow in the coming weeks."

Sports.title: 'Outstanding' Jacks 'growing in new role' after five-for vs Sri Lanka
Sports.content:
Will Jacks was hailed as "outstanding" by England white-ball captain Harry Brook on Tuesday night as he took five wickets to spur his side to an 89-run victory against Sri Lanka.

Jacks starred with both bat and ball as England took a 1-0 lead in the three-match ODI series, helping them reach 265 all out with an unbeaten 46 from 47 balls before claiming five wickets with the ball.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jacks took five wickets during England's 89-run victory against Sri Lanka

In the 48th over, the 27-year-old, who has been moved down the order, ruthlessly smashed Dushmantha Chameera for four consecutive fours, making a score of 18 off the over.

He was brought on to bowl in the 20th over of Sri Lanka's innings, and would end the day with career-best figures of 5-22 from seven overs.

"He's really growing into this role," Brook said of Jacks. "He's bought into everything that we want to do, as have the other boys.

Score summary - England vs Sri Lanka, first ODI, Durham England 265 in 48.1 overs (elected to bat): Harry Brook (67 off 69 balls), Will Jacks (46 off 47), Joe Root (44 off 52); Sachindu Colombage (3-44), Asitha Fernando (3-53) Sri Lanka 176 all out in 37 overs (chasing 266):Dunith Wellalage (45 off 36 balls), Kusal Mendis (42 off 60), Pathum Nissanka (27 off 37); Will Jacks (5-22), Jamie Overton (2-21)

"We're talking about all sorts of aspects of the game, trying to adapt to conditions, and he's done that exceptionally well since he's come back in over the last 18 months.

"He could have easily just moaned and groaned about batting in the middle-order and playing as an all-rounder, but he's really grown into that and accepted that's going to be his role for a period of time.

"He's been a very vital player. He's not a part-timer; he is a very good off-spinner. He proved that today. He can spin the ball big and contain batters when we need to."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England set Sri Lanka a score of 266 in the first innings before bowling out their opponents for 176

After Jacks first dismissed Charith Asalanka for one, England had struggled to remove Kusal Mendis, who brought up 42 from 60 deliveries. Jacks stepped up again to provide the breakthrough, trapping the Sri Lanka captain lbw in the 27th over.

Dunith Wellalage top-scored for Sri Lanka with 45 from 36 deliveries, but just as he closed in on his half-century, Jacks claimed his third wicket of the day. Two deliveries later, the England all-rounder removed Asitha Fernando for a duck.

Jacks then wrapped up England's victory with the delivery of the day, dismissing Dilshan Madushanka for nought with a sensational turning ball that crashed into the Sri Lankan bowler's stumps.

His figures are the best by an England spinner in an ODI since Vic Marks took 5-20 against New Zealand in Wellington in 1984.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jacks said he likes to approach each game with an open mind

"I go into each game with an open mind and see what it is when I walk out there," Jacks said when asked about batting down the order. "I think it's quite refreshing and it keeps me relaxed."

On his bowling, he added: "Having batted on the wicket and knowing what it was like, I knew I was going to play a decent role.

"Depending on what time you bowl, it doesn't really bother me. Harry [Brook] likes us to be as flexible as possible; that's why I think we're achieving some good things.

"No matter the time, you've just got to do your best."

Morgan: Jacks impressing in new role

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eoin Morgan praised the England allrounder for continuing to grow in his new position

Sky Sports Cricket's Eoin Morgan said:

"His clarity of thought in that role and the way he unpicks every situation is different from game to game.

"He's shown a fantastic attitude and wholeheartedly throws himself into every game. It's easy for an opener to come down the order and think, 'It's not my day.' But batting at five, six or seven is high-risk, high-reward.

"How you manage the early part of your innings is key to setting up the rest of it.

"Even at the start of his innings, Jacks felt like he was scratching around a little bit. But sticking in there and building a solid start allowed him to kick on.

"Today, he didn't come on to bowl as early as he would have liked because Rehan Ahmed took the ball first.

"He gets a huge amount of turn, and we even saw the couple of wides he bowled that he wasn't happy with. He was trying to be as miserly as possible.

"It was a great day for him. He continues to grow into that role, which is really good because it's a key role in ODI cricket."

Sports.title: Jacks stars as England beat Sri Lanka in first ODI
Sports.content:
England continued their white-ball dominance over Sri Lanka with an 89-run victory in Durham, taking a 1-0 lead in the three-match ODI series.

Will Jacks starred with bat and ball, hitting an handy 46 not out off 47 balls before completing a career-best 5-22 to wrap up the Sri Lankan tail.

Captain Harry Brook (67 off 69 balls) top-scored after electing to bat at the toss but a middle order wobble inspired by debutant Sachindu Colombage (3-44) restricted England to 265 in 48.1 overs.

England took steady wickets to hamper Sri Lanka's pursuit of 266 before Jacks struck three times in the final over as the tourists were bowled out for 176 in 37 overs.

Score summary - England vs Sri Lanka, first ODI, Durham England 265 in 48.1 overs (elected to bat): Harry Brook (67 off 69 balls), Will Jacks (46 off 47), Joe Root (44 off 52); Sachindu Colombage (3-44), Asitha Fernando (3-53) Sri Lanka 176 all out in 37 overs (chasing 266):Dunith Wellalage (45 off 36 balls), Kusal Mendis (42 off 60), Pathum Nissanka (27 off 37); Will Jacks (5-22), Jamie Overton (2-21)

England take ODI series lead over Sri Lanka

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sri Lankan bowler Avishka Fernando took the first wicket of the ODI match against England.

England's decision to bat first after winning the toss was immediately tested when Tom Banton fell to a jaffa from Asitha Fernando, the delivery nipping back to clip the bail on top of off stump.

The hosts weathered the early setback, with Joe Root sharing 50-run partnerships with Ben Duckett and Harry Brook to steer England to 135-2 after Duckett was trapped lbw by Dunith Wellalage.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Root was bowled out by Sachindu Colombage on his debut during the ODI match between England and Sri Lanka.

Root's 68-run stand with Brook was ended when he was deceived and bowled by the mystery spin of debutant Colombage, six runs short of his half-century.

The dismissal of England captain Brook, caught off the bowling of Dushmantha Chameera after reaching a seventh ODI century in 49 balls, sparked a middle-order collapse.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rehan Ahmed was run out after a fantastic piece of fielding by Sri Lanka during their ODI match against England.

Jos Buttler was trapped lbw before Rehan Ahmed was run out by a superb direct hit from Charith Asalanka. Jamie Overton, Gus Atkinson and Jofra Archer were then all bowled by Colombage, Dilshan Madushanka and Fernando respectively, as England lost six wickets for 65 runs in 15.5 overs.

Will Jacks led England's resistance with an unbeaten 46 from 47 balls, including an explosive 18 in the 48th over as the hosts moved beyond 250. But the late charge was cut short when Fernando produced a reverse-swinging yorker to clean up Josh Tongue.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sachindu Colombage took three wickets for Sri Lanka during their ODI match against England.

Sri Lanka negotiated the first five overs of their chase of 266 without alarm before Kamindu Mendis holed out to Duckett at short midwicket off Atkinson.

Tongue then accounted for Sri Lanka's other opener, inducing an edge through to wicketkeeper Buttler as the tourists slipped to 51-2.

Banton produced a stunning, sharp catch at extra cover to dismiss the driving Pavan Rathnayake, before Jacks trapped a sweeping Asalanka lbw three balls later to leave Sri Lanka 85-4 and in deep trouble.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Overton took a fantastic wicket during the England and Sri Lanka ODI.

Overton struck again three overs later, tempting Janith Liyanage into a loose waft outside off as he edged behind to leave Sri Lanka 100-5.

The writing was on the wall when captain Kusal Mendis was trapped lbw by Jacks, leaving Sri Lanka reeling at 105-6. Their woes deepened when Colombage suffered the same fate against Rehan Ahmed.

Wellalage led a brief Sri Lanka fightback, plundering 17 from an Ahmed over before his 42-run partnership with Chameera revived hopes at 133-7.

But Jacks extinguished those hopes in a decisive final over, removing Wellalage, Fernando and Madushanka to wrap up the victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Will Jacks took five wickets during England's win against Sri Lanka in the first ODI.

Jacks: A great all-round game

Player of the match Will Jacks (46no off 47) and 5-22 in 7 overs:

"It was a really good all-round performance from the team there.

"I am getting used to this role now. It is more about playing the situation and playing what is out there.

"Having batted on it and what it was like, I knew I was going to play a decent role.

"No matter the time, you have got to do your best."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England's Will Jacks reflected on a brilliant bowling display during the first ODI against Sri Lanka

Brook: Our communication was on point

England captain Harry Brook:

"It wasn't the easiest of surfaces but we want to be a team that can adapt to conditions. We did that well today.

"We knew exactly what we were going to do with the ball out there and we did that beautifully.

"I think the clarity we went out into the field with was outstanding. We communicated very well."
