World.title: Sudan: Drone Strikes Destroy More Than 330,000 Learning Materials in Sudan's North Kordofan State
World.content:
New York/Nairobi/Khartoum — Drone strikes on two warehouses in Shikan locality, North Kordofan, on 20 September destroyed over 292,000 school textbooks, 40,000 Arabic Language and Mathematics Review Books, and other learning materials intended for distribution to children.

The materials were to be distributed from October 2026, marking the start of the new school year, including to schools in West Bara, Bara and Um Dam, with the loss expected to affect the learning of thousands of children.

"The destruction of these learning materials is a setback for children at a time when every effort is being made to get them back into the classroom," said Angela Kearney, UNICEF Representative in Sudan. "Many children have missed years of schooling due to the conflict. With schools already facing shortages of teachers, desks and learning materials, this loss will further undermine children's access to quality education. Every child has the right to education, and that right must be protected."

Delivering education supplies to the conflict-affected areas in Sudan is often challenging, making the loss of these materials particularly significant. Access to safe learning opportunities remains essential to helping children learn, recover and build their futures.

UNICEF calls on all parties to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure and uphold their obligations under international humanitarian law. Education supplies and facilities must be safeguarded to ensure children can fulfill their right to education.

World.title: North Africa: Egypt Declares Suez Canal Secure As August Revenue Surges to $567 Million
World.content:
CAIRO — Egypt's Suez Canal Authority (SCA) has declared the waterway safe, with maritime traffic flowing normally as August revenue rose 56.7 percent year-on-year to $567.1 million, up from $326 million in the same month of 2025. SCA Chairman Osama Rabie announced the figures during a ceremony in Alexandria marking World Maritime Day 2026, organized by the Maritime Transport Sector of the Ministry of Transport.

The revenue increase represents a notable rebound for a canal that has endured significant disruptions in recent years. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty previously said Red Sea tensions had cost Egypt roughly $11 billion in lost Suez Canal income. The latest numbers point to a recovery for one of the country's most vital sources of foreign currency.

The canal transited 1,358 vessels in August 2026, a 27 percent increase from 1,070 vessels in August 2025. Net tonnage rose 51.1 per cent to 68.3 million tonnes, up from 45.2 million tonnes a year earlier.

Rabie emphasized that navigation remained stable and services continued at high efficiency. He added that canal pilots were carrying out their duties with the highest levels of readiness and professionalism.

Despite the strong year-on-year gains, traffic has not returned to pre-disruption levels. Average canal transits stood at about 40.8 vessels per day between January and August 2026, compared with 73.7 per day in 2023. Canal revenue reached $4.67 billion in fiscal year 2025/2026, a 23 percent increase, though vessel transits and cargo tonnage remain below the canal's peak performance.

The Suez Canal remains a critical artery for global trade, linking the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea and offering the shortest maritime route between Asia and Europe.

World.title: Liberia: A Decade On - the World Is Still Listening to Liberia's Ebola Story
World.content:
Ten years after Ebola swept through Liberia and claimed thousands of lives, the world is still turning to this small West African nation for answers. On Sunday, in a wide-ranging conversation, Chris McCall of The Lancet's World Report, the news section of one of the world's oldest and most trusted medical journals, sat down with Gregory T. Blamoh, Secretary General of the Liberia National Red Cross Society (LNRCS), to revisit an outbreak that reshaped the country's approach to public health emergencies.

The conversation was part of a broader examination of how nations once devastated by epidemics have turned hard-won experience into lasting institutional memory.

"Our success in the Ebola response was collective," Blamoh said. "Every Liberian was involved and learned from the response. Systems have been put in place, and every Liberian is fully aware of Ebola. And if we were to have any recurrence, the impact will not be as devastating as the first outbreak."

Community volunteers built that collective response on the ground, many mobilized through the LNRCS.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

During the 2014 outbreak, Red Cross volunteers trained, equipped, and trusted by their neighbors stood on the front lines, working across four areas of intervention that remain central to the organization's emergency work today: Safe and Dignified Burial, Risk Communication, Contact Tracing, and Psychosocial Support.

Ten years on, those four pillars remain embedded in Liberia's emergency preparedness architecture.

The LNRCS has continued training volunteers, strengthening early warning systems, and keeping communities informed work that has left the country better prepared for future public health emergencies.

Among the most sensitive and, at the time, most misunderstood interventions was Safe and Dignified Burial. Ebola spreads readily through contact with the bodies of the dead, making traditional burial practices a serious transmission risk.

Working in full protective equipment, 240 LNRCS-trained burial team members took on the difficult task of safely managing the remains of 3,820 Ebola victims while preserving as much dignity and cultural respect as possible.

It required constant, careful engagement with grieving families, community members, and traditional leaders, building the trust needed to explain why long-held burial practices had to change to protect the living.

Alongside the burial teams, Red Cross volunteers led sustained awareness campaigns, going house to house, market to market, and community to community to explain how the virus spread and how it could be stopped. In a crisis defined as much by fear and misinformation as by the disease itself, these conversations became one of the response's most powerful tools, correcting rumors, dispelling myths, and building trust.

Close 

The experience underscored a lesson that still shapes humanitarian response today: communities are not simply recipients of information, but essential partners in saving lives.

Volunteers also formed the backbone of contact tracing, systematically identifying and monitoring people who had been in contact with confirmed cases, following them through the 21-day incubation period, and alerting health authorities at the first sign of symptoms. This community-level monitoring helped catch potential cases early and contain chains of transmission before they could grow work that demanded discipline, persistence, and close coordination with health authorities.

The response also recognized the psychological toll of the outbreak on survivors, families, communities, and responders themselves.

Psychosocial support was woven into the Red Cross response, offering counseling and community-based care to help people navigate grief, stigma, fear, and trauma effects that, for many communities, lingered long after the outbreak was officially declared over.

A decade later, Liberia's Ebola experience continues to demonstrate the value of preparedness, community trust, local leadership, and volunteer action. The Red Cross volunteers at the center of the response were more than emergency workers; they were neighbors and trusted voices who translated public health messages into action that saved lives.

Today, the systems and community networks strengthened during the Ebola response continue to inform Liberia's readiness for future emergencies. As Blamoh put it, the experience "isn't just history; it's a roadmap other nations are learning from."

Ten years later, the world is still listening to Liberia. And Liberia's lessons still matter.

World.title: Nigeria: Central Bank Cuts Interest Rate
World.content:
"It emphasised that the recalibration of the corridor does not constitute a change in the current monetary policy stance, but rather an operational reset to enhance the effectiveness of monetary policy and support the transition to an inflation targeting framework," CBN said.

The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has cut the benchmark interest rate to 23 per cent.

CBN Governor Olayemi Cardoso disclosed the committee's decision at the conclusion of the bank's two-day, 307th Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting, held from 21 to 22 September in Abuja.

This decision followed two consecutive retention of the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 26.5 per cent, holding it in May and July previously, following a 50-basis-point reduction in February from 27 per cent.



Speaking after the meeting, the CBN Governor stated that the committee decided to reset the MPR and recalibrate the policy corridor as an important operational realignment aimed at strengthening monetary policy transmission.

"The committee decided to reset the MPR and recalibrate the policy corridor as an important operational realignment aimed at strengthening monetary policy transmission and reinforcing the primacy of the monetary policy rate.

"It emphasised that the recalibration of the corridor does not constitute a change in the current monetary policy stance, but rather an operational reset to enhance the effectiveness of monetary policy and support the transition to an inflation targeting framework," CBN said.

The MPC also adjusted the asymmetric facilities corridor around the MPR to +50/-300 basis points, a move aimed at discouraging banks from keeping idle funds with the CBN and encouraging increased lending into the economy.

Furthermore, the committee maintained the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) for commercial banks at 45 per cent, retained the rate for merchant banks at 16 per cent, and kept the CRR on non-TSA public-sector deposits at 75 per cent for liquidity management considerations.

CBN cut the interest rate amid its continued efforts to moderate Nigeria's headline inflation.

Since CBN maintained the rate in May, inflationary pressure has generally eased, with headline inflation standing at 15.39 per cent in August, down from 15.43 per cent in July, 15.91 per cent in June and 15.93 per cent in May, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS).

The rise in inflation recorded in April followed the escalation of the Middle East conflict, which began in February and contributed to higher global oil prices.

However, despite the recent easing in inflation, CBN's decision comes amid a renewed increase in fuel prices across the country, a development that could put fresh upward pressure on the prices of goods and services.

World.title: Kenya: Kenyatta Clears Way for New Jubilee Leadership
World.content:
Nairobi — Former President Uhuru Kenyatta has formally cleared the way for a leadership transition in the Jubilee Party, asking members to accept former Interior Cabinet Secretary Fred Matiang'i to take his place as the party prepares for the 2027 General Election.

Speaking during the Jubilee Party handover, Uhuru said he would move to a senior advisory role while remaining a member of the party.

He then publicly asked Jubilee members to back Matiang'i, who has already been endorsed by the party as its presidential candidate for the 2027 election.

"Let me take that upper position, to be like a senior advisor there," Uhuru said, adding that he would remain available to guide the party.



He told delegates that once he moved to the senior position, his "younger brother" should take over the position he had been occupying.

"And together with all our Jubilee delegates, let us now go and organize ourselves to give him the work for 2027," Uhuru said.

Uhuru made the message even clearer, directly asking Jubilee members to accept Matiang'i.

"I ask you with respect to accept and welcome him. You agreed that I move to that top position, right?" he told the delegates.

"And agree to welcome Fred Okeng'o Matiang'i to take my place. Will you accept that?"

The crowd responded in the affirmative.

Uhuru described Matiang'i as a young leader from Kisii with the qualities he believes Jubilee needs as it prepares for the next election.

"I see there is this young man from Kisii over there called Fred Matiang'i," Uhuru said.

He described him as a person with wisdom, hardworking and someone who "loves Kenyans" and has "no malice."

Uhuru also urged Jubilee members to begin organising early, saying the political season had already started.

He called for the party to identify candidates for elective positions across the country, including MCAs, governors, senators and MPs, as well as a presidential candidate.

"Let us go and look for a President who will lead us like this," Uhuru said.

Despite stepping aside from the top party position, Uhuru insisted that he was not abandoning Jubilee.

"Even now, me as I am, over there, and I'm going nowhere. I am still a Jubilee member," he said.

He said he would remain involved in the party and use his experience to advise its leadership.

"I want to join hands with you so we can organize ourselves," Uhuru said, adding that he had no interest in political insults and wanted Jubilee to work with other Kenyans.

Matiang'i welcomed the endorsement noting that the moment "is humbling."

Close 

"I am deeply humbled and the best gift that we can give Uhuru is ensure that we keep on with this party and its activities as we head to 2027," he said.

The move follows a High Court ruling that barred retired presidents from continuing to hold formal leadership positions in political parties beyond six months after leaving office. Uhuru had earlier said he was ready to facilitate a lawful handover in line with Jubilee's constitution.

The transition has already triggered competition within Jubilee, with Deputy Party Leader Jeremiah Kioni offering himself for the position of party leader and insisting that the next leader should be chosen through the party's democratic structures.

Uhuru, however, said the process should be about organising the party and preparing for 2027.

"Is it running away that I have run away, or is it organizing ourselves that we are organizing ourselves?" he asked.

He also urged Jubilee members to avoid political insults and instead explain to Kenyans what they intend to do if elected.

"Go and tell Kenyans how you will serve them," Uhuru said.

He added: "A vote is not a marketplace. A vote is a vision."

World.title: Three Word Game: Three words to describe every NFL team so far this season ahead of Week 3
World.content:
In life, it often takes just three words to tell a story. NFL teams are no different.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Today, we play to the OutKick-famous Three-Word Game to describe every NFL team after two weeks:

Detroit Lions (1-1): Defense is putrid.

The Lions’ defense ranks 31st in points and yards allowed. They have allowed 71 points through two games. The secondary is a mess and cannot pressure the quarterback.

Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard’s seat could and should get hot quickly.

Kansas City Chiefs (2-0): They are back.

The Chiefs have had an average offense over the past three seasons. Not this year. Through two games, Kansas City has the NFL’s top-ranked offense.

Free-agent addition Kenneth Walker has been the biggest move of the offseason. He leads the NFL in rushing yards (290) and all-purpose yards (369).

There are reasonable concerns about whether the Chiefs can sustain this pace, especially with left tackle Josh Simmons still out under mysterious circumstances.

For now, the Chiefs look back to their old ways.

New York Giants (1-1): Season’s probably over.

After Week 1, the Giants looked like a playoff team and a potential dark-horse contender. After Week 2, that all seems like a distant memory.

ESPN reported Tuesday that quarterback Jaxson Dart’s knee injury is worse than expected and that he is likely to miss the rest of the season. Backup Jameis Winston hardly looked playable in relief Monday night against the Rams.

Miami Dolphins (0-2): Arch? Chambliss? Mensah?

Challenge: Name five players on the Miami Dolphins.

MIAMI DOLPHINS ENTER FULL REBUILD WITH MALIK WILLIS AT QUARTERBACK AND JEFF HAFLEY AS HEAD COACH

We can’t either.

The Dolphins’ roster is the least talented in recent memory. It’s difficult to envision them missing out on one of the top quarterbacks in what is expected to be an elite 2027 draft class.

The options could include Arch Manning, Trinidad Chambliss or keeping Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah in Miami.

San Francisco 49ers (2-0): Better than expected.

The 49ers were not frequently mentioned among the NFL’s best teams entering the season. Through two weeks, they are clearly among them.

Remember, this team entered Week 18 last season with a chance to earn the NFC’s No. 1 seed despite injuries to multiple All-Pro players.

If San Francisco can remain reasonably healthy, it should again contend for the top seed. This roster is still loaded.

Cleveland Browns (1-1): Well, they won.

In the biggest upset of the season, the Browns edged the Buccaneers on Sunday after a lengthy late-fourth-quarter weather delay.

Browns fans may have preferred another poor performance from Deshaun Watson. Instead, his 238-yard, two-touchdown, zero-interception performance will likely buy him at least a few more weeks as the starter.

FROM THE CHARGERS TO THE COLTS AND FALCONS, WHICH OF THE NFL'S EIGHT WINLESS TEAMS ARE ALREADY IN PANIC MODE

Buffalo Bills (2-0): No, it’s different.

Yes, the Bills have been Super Bowl champions in September for most of Josh Allen’s career, only to lose in heartbreaking fashion in January.

But this time does feel different.

Under head coach Joe Brady, Buffalo has the NFL’s highest-scoring offense and has turned tight end Dalton Kincaid into the league’s best pass-catching option.

The Bills may not have the marquee names of the Rams, but their roster is among the league’s most complete. Notably, edge rusher Greg Rousseau leads the NFL with four sacks and may have elevated his game from good to great.

Atlanta Falcons (0-2): Can’t flex yet.

Unfortunately, networks cannot flex games out of prime time this early in the season. Therefore, the Falcons will be forced to perform on national television each of the next three weeks.

Minnesota Vikings (2-0): The Northern favorites.

The Vikings entered the season with the lowest odds of winning what was expected to be a vaunted NFC North. Suddenly, concerns about the Lions’ defense, the Packers’ roster and Caleb Williams’ health have made Minnesota the betting favorite to win the division.

Further, the Vikings have the talent to justify it.

Las Vegas Raiders (2-0): Just LIKE that.

Just like that, the Raiders are 2-0 and have formed the NFL’s best pass-blocking line, according to ESPN Stats & Information.

Brock Bowers, the Raiders’ best player, is also expected to make his season debut Sunday.

The schedule gets tougher from here. Las Vegas’ next five opponents are the Saints, Chiefs, Patriots, Bills and Rams. Winning two of those matchups would seem like a victory for this team.

Houston Texans (0-2): Not worried, yet.

The Texans started 0-3 last season and finished 12-5. There is no reason to panic just yet.

That said, Houston’s highly acclaimed defense has not been nearly as strong this season. The Texans rank 20th in yards allowed and 24th in points allowed.

Playing Josh Allen and Joe Burrow in consecutive weeks can do that to a defense. But C.J. Stroud is not good enough to lead this team into the postseason if the defense is anything short of dominant.

Philadelphia Eagles (2-0): Fly, Eagles … fly?

The good news: The Eagles are 2-0.

The bad news: They do not look particularly effective on either side of the ball.

The jury is still out in Philadelphia. Fortunately, the Eagles may face the Bears on Monday with Case Keenum starting at quarterback.

Los Angeles Rams (1-1): Super Bowl favorites.

Forget what happened in Australia. The Rams have the best roster in the NFL.

Aaron Donald looked like Aaron Donald on Monday night. Myles Garrett, Puka Nacua and Donald have not even shared the field yet.

Barring injury, the Rams should remain Super Bowl favorites throughout the season.

Tennessee Titans (0-2): So, so close.

The Titans looked like they had the Eagles, then they didn’t. Cam Ward still has a ways to go. It’s early, but so far, Carnell Tate has not lived up to his status as the fourth overall pick.

Still, Tennessee should have an opportunity to win its first game this week against a Jaxson Dart-less Giants team.

Dallas Cowboys (1-1): Waiting to see.

The Dallas Cowboys have as good an offense as any team in the NFL. The question is how much last year’s historically bad defense has improved. They looked better Sunday against the Commanders once Daniels went down.

Through two games, the team has yet to record a sack.

This team could go either way.

Carolina Panthers (1-1): Bryce is cooking.

Imagine telling anyone after their rookie seasons that Bryce Young would be better than Stroud. And yet, that is the case after the past two seasons.

The Panthers have scored 71 points in two games. That’s second-best in the NFL.

Seattle Seahawks (2-0): They can repeat.

Few teams received less hype about potentially repeating as Super Bowl champions in the offseason than the Seattle Seahawks. But they can.

The roster is well-rounded, they play fierce defense, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba is nearly unguardable. The Seahawks have even turned Drew Lock into a serviceable quarterback this season.

That’s impressive.

Baltimore Ravens (1-1): Not this again.

For what seems like the fifth year in a row, the Ravens dominated Week 1, and the national media rushed to anoint them the top team in the AFC and Lamar Jackson the MVP frontrunner.

Then, as usual, the team suffered a major letdown in Week 2 against the Saints, culminating in a game-losing interception thrown by Jackson.

They never learn.

They being the media.

Denver Broncos (1-1): Week 1 lies.

As always, Week 1 lies to us. Week 1 told us the Denver Broncos were a poorly coached team with holes on both sides of the ball.

Week 2 tends to be more truthful and showed us the opposite.

The Denver Broncos are really good. The addition of Jaylen Waddle showed on Sunday.

New York Jets (1-1): Maybe not hopeless.

The Jets are not good, but they are not completely hopeless, either. That qualifies as progress in New York.

They should be 2-0.

Cincinnati Bengals (2-0): They play defense.

The Bengals deviated from strategy this offseason and paid for a defense. It’s working. Two weeks in, the Bengals are pressuring the quarterback and forcing teams off the field.

If that continues, the Bengals can beat anyone.

Now, if Joe Burrow could stay healthy …

Arizona Cardinals (1-1): The real LaFleur.

The Cardinals are, dare we say, competitive.

Between Trey McBride, Jeremiyah Love and Michael Wilson, Arizona has a puncher’s chance against most opponents. First-year coach Mike LaFleur is impressive.

Pittsburgh Steelers (1-1): Same old Steelers.

Pittsburgh remains well-coached, physical, and offensively limited. The Steelers are exactly what everyone expected and exactly what they seemingly are every season.

They are also so boring to watch.

Jacksonville Jaguars (1-1): Another false alarm.

The Jaguars briefly looked like a contender. Then reality returned. Jacksonville still has too many holes to be taken seriously.

Chicago Bears (1-1): The crisis averted.

It sounds like Caleb Williams will miss a game or two because of a hamstring injury. But if you told the Bears that and a week of crying-Caleb memes was the worst-case scenario after how bad his injury looked, they would take it.

The Bears will be fine.

Los Angeles Chargers (0-2): Not getting better.

The Chargers are 0-2. The offense and defense look confused. The offensive line is once again a weakness. Jim Harbaugh looks befuddled on the sideline.

None of it makes much sense.

Worst of all, the Chargers’ next seven opponents are the Buffalo Bills, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos, Kansas City Chiefs, Los Angeles Rams, Houston Texans, and Baltimore Ravens.

What’s the best-case scenario here? A 1-8 start?

New England Patriots (1-1): Much-improved defense.

The Patriots’ offense has struggled. A.J. Brown is hurt, and stud right guard Mike Onwenu is out for the season. However, the defense is much improved from last season.

The team has allowed only 16 points through two games against the Seahawks and Steelers.

Drake Maye must play better, though.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-2): Very, very disappointing?

Two weeks into this season, the Bucks are one of the NFL's biggest disappointments. They lost to the Browns.

The talent is there, but they need to win three of their next five against the Vikings, Packers, Cowboys, Steelers, and Panthers.

We aren't sure they will do it.

Green Bay Packers (1-1): Well, they survived.

The Packers survived a double-digit deficit to the Jets on Sunday to avoid a 0-2 start.

In doing so, Green Bay became the first team since 1941 to win a game while recording fewer than 200 yards of offense, 100-plus penalty yards and a negative turnover margin.

The team is not clicking and may need to keep surviving until Micah Parsons and Josh Jacobs return.

Indianapolis Colts (0-2): Last-ranked defense.

The Colts’ offense was impressive in an overtime loss to the Chiefs. However, the defense has been horrendous.

Through two weeks, the Colts’ defense has given up 1,029 total yards, which ranks last in the NFL, along with 675 passing yards, also last, 354 rushing yards, second-to-last, and 74 points, last.

That’s a problem.

New Orleans Saints (1-1): No Shoughs given.

The Saints might have the best quarterback most of the public has never heard of: Tyler Shough. He leads the league in passing yards and firmly outplayed Lamar Jackson head-to-head Sunday.

The touted rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson is expected to make his season debut next month, giving Shough another option.

In the NFC South, the Saints are a playoff-caliber team — and one with firepower.

Washington Commanders (0-2): He’s hurt again.

Jayden Daniels is hurt again. This roster isn’t good enough to overcome annual injuries to a quarterback who makes everything work.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Beyond this season, the question will soon become whether Washington can extend Daniels given his injury history.

World.title: Costco food court item packs more protein than anything else on the menu, but there's a catch
World.content:

One of Costco's newer food court additions is packing more protein than anything else on the menu — but a dietitian says shoppers should look beyond the eye-catching number.

The Rotisserie Chicken Chef Salad, which Costco highlighted among its new food court offerings this year, contains 59 grams of protein along with 840 calories.

The $7.99 salad includes rotisserie chicken, hard-boiled eggs, bacon bits and shredded cheddar cheese on a bed of romaine lettuce, along with tomatoes and creamy peppercorn ranch dressing.

COSTCO BRINGS BACK A FAN-FAVORITE FOOD COURT TREAT AFTER YEARS OFF THE MENU

Jamie Lee McIntyre, a Florida-based registered dietitian nutritionist, told Fox News Digital that protein is only one factor consumers should consider when deciding what to eat.

"That's just a nutrition attribute," McIntyre said of protein. She noted that "a food can be high in protein, but it can also still be high in sodium, saturated fat or calories."

Regarding this particular Costco menu item, McIntyre said the protein "is coming from some good whole foods, chicken and eggs. There's veggies in there. So those are some good building blocks of the meal. But I would say, for a lot of people, 840 calories might be a bit much for a light lunch."

COSTCO SHOPPERS CHALLENGE INFLUENCER'S CLAIM THAT 'INSANE' CHICKEN MEAL CAN FEED FAMILY OF FIVE

Other Costco food court options aren't far behind the chef salad when it comes to protein.

The Chicken Caesar Salad contains 58 grams of protein, just one gram less than the Rotisserie Chicken Chef Salad.

The Chicken Bake is another high-protein option, with 53 grams.

World.title: Missouri mom who put newborn in oven instead of crib learns fate as murder charge dropped
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A Missouri mother who said she accidentally put her 1-month-old baby in an oven instead of a crib will spend more than a decade behind bars after reaching a deal that wiped away a first-degree murder charge.

Mariah Thomas, 28, pleaded guilty Tuesday to first-degree endangering the welfare of a child resulting in death and was ordered to serve 13 years in the Missouri Department of Corrections, according to Jackson County court records.

The punishment came more than two years after Kansas City police found Thomas' infant daughter dead with severe burns inside a city home.

NEW MEXICO WOMAN'S BODYCAM CONFESSION ABOUT HIDING NEWBORN BABY IN HOSPITAL GARBAGE TOSSED BY STATE COURT

Thomas was also charged with first-degree murder, but that count was dismissed as part of the plea agreement, court records show. She received no probation and will be credited for time already served.

The nightmare unfolded on Feb. 9, 2024, after officers were called to the home around 1:30 p.m. on charges involving a report of a baby who was not breathing, according to charging documents.

Police arrived to find the 1-month-old child with apparent burns across her body. Kansas City Fire Department personnel pronounced her dead at the scene.

Investigators were told Thomas had gone to put her daughter down for a nap but "accidentally placed her in the oven instead of the crib," the documents state.

FLORIDA 3-YEAR-OLD DIES AFTER TRAGIC INCIDENT INVOLVING COMMON PLAY TOY AT BABYSITTER'S HOUSE

A family member later told detectives that Thomas said, "I thought I put [her] in her crib and I accidentally put her in the oven."

The child was wearing a bodysuit over a diaper, and investigators said her clothing appeared to have melted onto the diaper. Police also recovered a baby blanket with significant burn marks from the living room, according to the probable cause statement.

The infant was identified by FOX 4 Kansas City as Za'riah Thomas.

Thomas initially declined to speak with detectives after being advised of her rights, but she agreed to provide a blood sample and allow investigators to access data from her cellphone, the documents state.

STARVING TODDLER ATE DIAPERS AND DRYWALL BEFORE DYING IN FILTHY ROOM WHILE PARENTS LIVED CLEAN, POLICE SAY

Then-Jackson County Prosecutor Jean Peters Baker called the child's death a "gruesome" tragedy when the original charge was announced in February 2024.

"We acknowledge the gruesome nature of this tragedy, and our hearts are weighted by the loss of this precious life," Baker said at the time. "We trust the criminal justice system to respond appropriately to these awful circumstances."

The original complaint charged Thomas only with first-degree endangering the welfare of a child resulting in death.

Court records show prosecutors later added the first-degree murder count that was ultimately dismissed under Tuesday's agreement.

NORTH DAKOTA MOM STABS HER 2 CHILDREN TO DEATH IN 'HORRIFIC' KILLING THAT LEFT COPS TRAUMATIZED: OFFICIALS

Judge Sarah A. Castle found Thomas entered the guilty plea freely and voluntarily and understood the charge and consequences. The judgment states Thomas had no mental disease or defect defense.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Thomas was returned to the Jackson County sheriff’s custody to await transfer to state prison. The judge also ordered her to pay $68 to Missouri’s Crime Victims’ Compensation Fund and waived all other court costs.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Jackson County prosecutor's office for comment.

World.title: Bodycam footage captures moments after ICE shooting of Venezuelan migrant in Austin
World.content:

The Austin Police Department on Tuesday released body camera footage showing the arrest of an illegal Venezuelan immigrant who was shot moments earlier by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers over the weekend.

Three short videos detail the local police response to the shooting of 28-year-old Wilber Rafael Garces Perez on Sunday as ICE officers attempted to take him into custody.

In one video, what sounds like three gunshots can be heard. Another clip shows an officer arriving at the scene, where Garces Perez is seen sitting hunched over in the driver's seat of his vehicle and appearing to grab his left shoulder in pain.

DEM REACTIONS WITHIN MOMENTS OF AUSTIN ICE SHOOTING SPARK VIRAL OUTRAGE LOCALLY, ONLINE: 'DISQUALIFYING'

Officers wearing body cameras assisted Garces Perez out of the vehicle, contradicting claims that he was dragged out by agents, before placing him under arrest.

Another officer is heard ordering someone to get a pair of shears to cut open Garces Perez's shirt to examine his wounds.

ICE RESUMES NATIONWIDE TRAFFIC STOPS UNDER NEW POLICY REQUIRING BODY CAMERAS

"¿Tiene armas?" an officer asks in Spanish, inquiring if Garces Perez has any firearms.

"No," Garces Perez replies.

"He's got… looks like one gunshot wound so far," an officer is heard saying.

Garces Perez was reportedly delivering a DoorDash order when he made a U-turn under a highway before ICE agents continued to pursue him. His attorney, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, claimed an unmarked truck chased her client and sideswiped his vehicle before he was shot.

SOCIALIST, COMMUNIST GROUPS COORDINATE, PROMOTE 'SPONTANEOUS' ANTI-ICE PROTESTS IN AUSTIN

Authorities confirmed Garces Perez had a final order of removal. However, Lincoln-Goldfinch said her client received the order after a hearing notice was sent to his previous address, despite him having updated his address with the court.

ICE has disputed rumors surrounding the shooting and Garces Perez's legal status, noting that his work permit expired in 2025 and that holding one does not confer legal status in the United States.

The agency also stated that Garces Perez was released from the hospital and arrived at an ICE detention facility just hours later, where he slept on a bed. ICE rebuffed allegations that Garces Perez was indiscriminately targeted.

"This illegal alien was the subject of a targeted vehicle stop," ICE said in a statement. "What makes someone a target for immigration enforcement is whether or not they are illegally in the U.S. Resisting officers and evading arrest is dangerous for our officers, illegal aliens, and the public. We remind the public that resisting officers and evading arrest is a felony and a federal crime. Sanctuary politicians need to stop encouraging this dangerous behavior that puts our officers and the public at risk."

World.title: Florida woman reaches plea deal after months behind bars for allegedly having drugs fall out of 'jail purse'
World.content:
A plea deal has been struck between prosecutors and a Florida woman who allegedly had drugs placed in her "jail purse" by someone during an intimate encounter. That was her story anyway.

Reagan Cox was arrested in late June on charges of resisting an officer without violence during a traffic stop. At the time, the Brevard County Sheriff's Office's social media announcement didn’t mention the reason for the stop.

Sheriff Wayne Ivey, I assume, was more concerned with telling the story of how the 30-year-old had introduced contraband into a jail using her butt. Understandable, but we have those details now.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

We now know that officers said she was "failing to maintain a single lane of travel" prior to being pulled over. They claimed she was "slow" and "lethargic" and that they smelled "the odor of burnt marijuana."

Cox was in court Tuesday and The Smoking Gun reports that she entered pleas to the charges of introducing contraband into a jail and obstruction. Prosecutors dropped a drug possession count.

World.title: Beyond killer robots: China's real AI threat to America is already here, experts warn
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

While Americans brace for a futuristic AI war of killer robots and bioweapons, experts warn ahead of President Xi Jinping's U.S. visit this week that Beijing is already actively undermining America's global supremacy through AI without ever firing a shot.

Experts who spoke with Fox News Digital outlined a stealthy, three-part playbook, which includes extracting the logic of American models, undercutting U.S. developers with free open-source software, and ultimately weaponizing those systems for things like cognitive warfare. They laid out how China bypasses billions of dollars in U.S. research through labs that interrogate cutting-edge American AI and copy its capabilities, while simultaneously flooding the global market with free alternatives.

"I think a ‘race’ is the wrong metaphor for this," Leah Siskind, an AI research fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital. "I think it's kind of like a multi-front war. And in some places, we're winning and some places we're losing."

XI PREPARES CHINA ‘FOR BATTLE’ AS EXPERT WARNS OF GRAVE DANGER FACING US AHEAD OF DC SUMMIT

While top American tech firms have poured billions into building ultra-expensive, proprietary systems, China has focused heavily on distributing free, open-source models across the globe. Siskind warned that because American tech is costly and the U.S. sector has largely neglected open-source investment, many Fortune 500 companies are making the financial choice to run their operations on Chinese models—unwittingly opening the door to potential CCP censorship, hidden backdoors and, ultimately, global dominance.

"How can you compete with something that's free when American tech is very, very expensive?" Siskind said. "How can we ensure that a Chinese open-source model would be truly clean, that it'd be truly free of CCP censorship? We can't be—we just wouldn't know. And that's by design. We wouldn't know what sort of trick backdoors might be implanted and how that could rear its head later on."

Meanwhile, China expert Gordon Chang warned that Beijing is intentionally using these free models to repeat an economic tactic it previously deployed to corner a different industry.

"This is a tactic that China used with solar panels," Chang told Fox News Digital. "Beijing sees that one day it will drive out the American models on cost and availability, and they will then dominate global AI."

CHAD WOLF: CONGRESS HAS A CHANCE TO STOP CHINA FROM TURNING YOUR CAR INTO A CHINESE SPY



But to flood the market with free software, Beijing first needs the underlying technology—and a way to bypass America's massive lead in computing power.

Chang noted that the U.S. possesses a commanding lead in physical infrastructure, boasting over 5,400 data centers compared to China's roughly 450, along with far superior microchips. To work around the staggering hardware and energy costs required to train artificial intelligence from scratch, Siskind warned that Chinese labs are closing the gap through a process known as "knowledge distillation"—a method where a smaller model essentially interrogates a larger, smarter American model to copy its logic.

"They are able to leapfrog the process by kind of stealing this information," Siskind said, pointing to the Chinese model DeepSeek as a prime example. "This is how they were able to release models like DeepSeek in 2025, which was seismic news because they were able to show that they were really competing with cutting-edge American models and had invested a fraction of the resources."

US ADVERSARY TURNS UP THE HEAT ON AMERICA’S AI LEAD WITH AN UNDERESTIMATED EDGE

The threat is not theoretical. Just last week, the Department of Homeland Security issued a joint cybersecurity advisory warning that Chinese companies are conducting "industrial-scale knowledge distillation campaigns" to extract proprietary capabilities from U.S. frontier models.

Beyond economic undercutting and software theft, the experts also warned Beijing is simultaneously deploying artificial intelligence into physical supply chains and public influence campaigns.

Rather than sci-fi "killer robots," Siskind emphasized that China's immediate physical priority is "embodied AI"—embedding artificial intelligence into real-world infrastructure like factory automation, commercial drones, and autonomous supply chains. Meanwhile, Chang warned that AI-enhanced propaganda poses a direct threat to American decision-making and democratic sovereignty.

"They're very good at cognitive warfare, and they can enhance their capabilities with artificial intelligence," Chang said. "We do not want our elections determined in China. We do not want our critical national security decisions being made in Beijing. And that's not impossible."

CHINA EXPERT WARNS BEIJING WANTS AMERICANS — NOT THE CCP — TO SPREAD ITS MESSAGE

As President Xi Jinping arrives in the U.S. this week, the experts who spoke to Fox News Digital said the White House must treat these non-cinematic threats with the same urgency as traditional military posturing.

To protect America's remaining edge, Siskind said Washington must tighten chip export loopholes, blacklist foreign labs engaging in deceptive distillation, and incentivize U.S. open-source development—emphasizing that "it is very important that the most advanced systems are developed under democracy and represent democratic values, as opposed to authoritarian values."

CHINA-LINKED HACKERS INFILTRATED US GOVERNMENT NETWORKS BEFORE FBI TAKEDOWN

For Chang, the stakes of that technological defense extend far beyond standard economic competition.

"Xi Jinping throughout this century has been pushing the Chinese imperial-era notion of Tianxia, or 'all under heaven'—that China's rulers have a right to rule the world," Chang warned. "That sounds ludicrous to us, but a Chinese regime powered by AI might actually be able to accomplish that. We certainly do not want our decisions being made in the Chinese capital."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Addressing the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, President Donald Trump reiterated Washington's goal of outpacing China, declaring that U.S. government documents will now refer to AI as "superintelligence."

"The United States totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control the artificial intelligence being spoken of," Trump told world leaders. "Whoever wins superintelligence wins. And we're leading now over China by a lot and everyone else. And we're going to keep it that way."

World.title: Trump’s focus on the press distracts Republicans from pocketbook issues
World.content:
WASHINGTON — Zigzagging from issue to issue, President Donald Trump has left his political allies struggling to keep pace with his pronouncements and lost precious time to drive a compelling message ahead of the midterm congressional elections, Republican strategists and people who’ve worked with him said.

The takeaway from recent polling is that voters worry most about high prices and the cost of living. But Trump has at times veered off pocketbook issues and made moves that are peripheral to the top-of-mind concerns of voters who will soon decide which party controls Congress.

The latest instance of Trump stepping on his party’s own messaging came on Friday.

In the hour before he held an Oval Office event focused on reducing prescription drug prices, Trump announced he was barring three news outlets from the White House grounds because he disliked their coverage. That caught even some members of his own staff off guard.

The media ban has dominated the news cycle for days, and rather than steer the conversation back to the savings Americans would reap from his policies, Trump amplified the furor.

Some Republican candidates in competitive races are increasingly distancing themselves from the president, believing that voters want a different focus and tack than what Trump is offering.

Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar, R-Fla., who is typically a staunch Trump defender, released an ad criticizing Trump’s mass deportation agenda. And GOP candidates in Iowa and Michigan have spoken out against the Iran war and its effect on prices.

Nearly two-thirds of adults lack confidence in the national news media, according to an NBC News survey in June sponsored by More Perfect, a nonpartisan nonprofit dedicated to advancing democracy. That makes the press a ripe target, though it isn’t clear that Americans want Trump to do something about it.

In an NBC News poll this month, registered voters cited inflation, government corruption, threats to democracy, jobs and the economy, the Iran war, immigration and healthcare costs as issues that loom largest; news coverage was not presented as an option.

“The president is out there touting his new arch,” Maura Gillespie, a Republican strategist, said of Trump’s plan to build a soaring arch near Arlington National Cemetery. “None of that addresses the gas prices being over $4. None of that addresses the younger voters who are struggling to afford their first home. None of that is landing.”

“Republicans need to steer their messaging away from Trump and divert their lane from him and focus on their constituents, because that’s the only thing that’s going to get them elected,” she added.

Trump often complains that news coverage fails to credit him for his successes. Labor and stock markets have proved resilient in Trump’s term, though wages are lagging inflation.

“The story no one is writing is how well the economy is doing in spite of the president’s lack of discipline,” said a person close to the administration, who added that Trump, 80, is growing “more impulsive with age.”

Speaking at the United Nations on Tuesday, Trump spooled out a list of accomplishments on his watch. He struck a triumphal tone as he cast the U.S. as a nation in the midst of a renaissance.

“Our economy is the envy of the world,” he said. “Our military is the most powerful on earth. Our technology is second to none and we’re leading in virtually everything. Our energy is fueling the planet. America is rising, our nation is growing, our power is expanding, our country is doing better than ever before.”

A White House spokesman, Kush Desai, said in a statement: “The Trump administration has remained laser-focused delivering on the president’s long-term economic agenda on the home front. Continued private-sector job growth, booming investments, and month-over-month prices of beef, chicken, prescription drugs, and other essentials declining in the last two inflation reports are all proof that America’s positive economic momentum continues.”

In recent months, Trump has slalomed back and forth through the issues.

In April, he threatened to destroy Iran’s civilization. Hours later, he backed off. He called Iran’s leaders “very rational” in June, “scum” in July. In his United Nations speech, Trump revived his apocalyptic threat. He warned that he may need to “annihilate” Iran and “drive them into hell” if the regime doesn’t agree to a deal to end the war.

This month he announced that he would send every American a $5,000 check if Republicans win the midterm elections; a key Republican senator whose committee oversees spending plans told reporters he had seen no details of how Trump’s idea would work.

“He’s very unpredictable. He calls it trusting his gut,” a second Republican senator told NBC News, who, like others in this piece, requested anonymity to speak candidly.

The press ban

The latest thunderclap from Trump’s social media feed was his eviction of CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House grounds.

A number of high-level White House aides were unaware beforehand that Trump had imposed the ban, and they struggled to explain it in the hours after it went into effect, according to conversations with four White House officials. Trump’s chief of staff Susie Wiles was absent from the building Friday when he announced the new directive, according to a person familiar with the situation, potentially leading to some of the confusion from the staff.

Still, aides sought to defend Trump’s move.

“Nobody close to the president was surprised at his action to hold the fake news accountable,” a senior White House official said.

Even Vice President JD Vance seemed at a loss as to how to explain the policy. Trump said specifically that he was “banning” the three outlets. But Vance, speaking to reporters Monday before heading to a campaign stop in North Carolina, said: “So, he’s not banning media outlets. What he’s doing is saying, ‘We’re not going to give you special access to the White House if you engage in what is effectively propaganda.’”

01:21 Rubio defends White House media outlet ban 00:00 00:00

In an interview with the “TODAY” show, Secretary of State Marco Rubio was asked whether media outlets should be banned because Trump doesn’t like their coverage. Rubio defended the president’s decision, saying, “There aren’t a bunch of police officers or soldiers kicking down the doors of MSNBC or MS NOW, whatever it’s called, and arresting people and unplugging it from the grid. They’re just not allowed to work from the workspace at the White House.”

MS NOW reporter Akayla Gardner, CNN’s Betsy Klein and Politico’s Cheyenne Haslett were all denied access to the White House on Saturday.

Klein and Haslett both had their White House press credentials confiscated when they sought to enter the grounds.

In his remarks Friday, Trump said, “We are banning them, yes we are, and there may be others to follow.” But a Trump adviser told NBC News on Tuesday “there are not” conversations happening inside the White House about expanding the ban to other disfavored outlets.

The TV networks have set up what’s known as a “pool”; they take turns covering the president as he goes about his public activities and sharing footage with other news outlets. CNN was supposed to provide TV pool coverage on Monday, but the White House barred them from their duties.

In response, the four other networks that are part of the TV network pool — NBC, ABC, CBS and Fox — refused to step in for the exiled CNN, meaning there was no TV pool coverage.

The repercussions were soon evident, potentially impeding Trump’s ability to deliver his message. Newsmax, a conservative outlet, tried to air the president’s remarks at a ribbon-cutting ceremony, but he couldn’t be heard.

“There’s no microphone because the pool cameras aren’t there. So maybe, Tim, this is one example of it backfiring just a little bit,” the Newsmax host said, adding, “So obviously, the ramifications are here. Can’t hear what the president is saying.”

Signs in solidarity with news organizations on the media ban list were placed in the White House press quarters on Saturday. Megan Shannon / NBC News

Trump’s ban is now before a judge. All three outlets filed suit against Trump on Monday, arguing that their eviction violates both due process rights and First Amendment protections for newsgathering and speech. U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly, a Trump appointee, set a hearing for Wednesday afternoon on the plaintiff’s motion for a temporary restraining order.

Trump has long lamented his media coverage. During his first term, the White House barred a CNN reporter, Jim Acosta, from the grounds following a contentious public exchange with Trump. CNN sued and the judge in the case — also Kelly — ordered the Trump administration to return Acosta’s press pass. In the end, the administration relented and restored the pass permanently.

In the new term, Trump has also talked privately about barring individual reporters and news outlets from the White House, but he refrained, according to two people familiar with those discussions.

By acting now, he may be distracting from a promising message for his party ahead of the midterms. Internal White House polling shows that Trump’s effort to reduce the cost of prescription drugs is his most popular issue, according to a White House official.

“He can and should be talking about the things that voters say are really important to them. And this [the media ban] is not it,” said Douglas Heye, a former communications director for the Republican National Committee. “It seems to have come out of nowhere and it seems to have caught a lot of people by surprise.”

“We’re less than 45 days out from the election and for the last three days no voter has heard anything about what Donald Trump wants to do to lower prices,” he added. “That’s a problem for any Republican on the ballot.”

The second Republican senator rattled off a series of issues that he’d like to see Trump spotlight.

“He can go out and talk about the reduction in crime,” the senator said, “or controlling the border, or eliminating rules and regulations.”

“But he’s probably not.”

‘Be quiet’

A recent run of setbacks has soured the mood inside the West Wing, a senior White House official said. Even though Trump now has a handpicked chairman of the Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh, the board defied Trump’s wishes last week and raised interest rates.

The Supreme Court has blocked Trump’s attempt to use the Postal Service to restrict mail-in voting ahead of the midterms, something Trump had hoped to do.

Gas prices have spiked since the Trump administration and Israel launched the war against Iran on Feb. 28, creating a slow-rolling backlash within the GOP.

Growing numbers of Republicans in tight midterm races are finding ways to distance themselves from Trump, whose approval rating in a new NBC News poll stood at 41%, a second-term low.

Rep. Ashley Hinson, an Iowa Republican who faces a tough race for the Senate, called for an “immediate end” to the Iran war in a social media post Monday. That’s an about-face from Hinson, who has voted against resolutions directing Trump to stop the war six different times.

“Iowans are being squeezed and shouldn’t have to foot the bill at the pump or the checkout line for the war in Iran,” Hinson wrote. “We need to use every option at our disposal to provide some relief from high prices.”

On Friday, Trump got some unsolicited advice from an iconic figure in the cultural world. Pat Boone, the 92-year-old singer-songwriter, released a video on X that offered a heartfelt suggestion to the president.

“Right now, I feel like you’re very tired,” Boone said, looking straight at the camera. “And I’m worried that many of us haven’t prayed enough for you because I think you’re wearing out and you’re feeling the pressure and expressing yourself in ways that are not becoming to you — that are not presidential.”

“So may I recommend something very highly: that you be quiet.”

World.title: ‘Looksmaxxing’ influencer Clavicular charged with rape of teen girl
World.content:
“Looksmaxxing” influencer Clavicular has been charged in connection with the rape of a teenage girl at his family’s house in Cape Cod last May, according to a criminal complaint.

Clavicular, 20, whose real name is Braden Peters, was charged with rape, drugging someone for sexual intercourse and procuring liquor for someone under 21 years old. The complaint was filed on Sept. 8 in Orleans District Court in Barnstable County, Massachusetts.

Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza, an 18-year-old influencer known online as Alorah or Alorah Ziva, alleged that in May 2025, while she was in Massachusetts, Peters called her an Uber to his family’s Cape Cod house. Once there, he got her drunk on vodka while they livestreamed on Twitch and then raped her, according to a criminal complaint from the Chatham Police Department. His mom and grandmother were allegedly in the house.

00:19 Clavicular charged with rape and drugging in Massachusetts 00:00 00:00

The charges come months after Mendoza sued Peters in Miami, accusing him of sexual battery in connection with the events of May 2025. The civil lawsuit also separately alleges he injected her face with a non-FDA-approved fat-dissolving substance during a November livestream in Florida.

A source familiar with the matter confirmed that the charges against Peters are in connection with Mendoza’s allegations.

Peters’ attorney at the time Mendoza’s civil lawsuit was filed said that he denies the allegations and “intends to vigorously defend himself.” The influencer defended himself in a series of posts on X on Monday night; he included a section of a video Mendoza previously posted in which she spoke about meeting Peters in May 2025 and called him “super nice.” Peters also shared what appears to be a handwritten letter Mendoza sent him, in which she said she was “thankful for you helping me.”

“How about dont finance cars you cant afford,” he wrote in one post. “Happens to all successful young men, people try to come for your money. Greed is evil.”

Mendoza’s lawyer told NBC News they have “no comment at this time as the police are handling the criminal matter.” Peters’ attorneys declined to comment.

The Bulwark first reported the criminal charges. Peters’ representative, Mitchell Jackson, said the outlet was “exaggerating” in its article and that Peters had not been served with an arrest warrant. An email to the general mailbox of The Bulwark seeking comment was not immediately returned late Monday.

“Braden Peters has not been physically served. As usual the Bulwark is exaggerating,” Jackson said in a text message Monday night. A source familiar with the matter confirmed that Peters had not been served as of Tuesday morning.

According to the Massachusetts criminal complaint, Mendoza told police she met Peters on Instagram in May 2025, while Mendoza was a minor, and they developed an online business relationship. Her civil lawsuit alleges that Peter offered to help make Mendoza well known online, and paid her $1,000 to make four “looksmaxxing” videos.

Eventually, the criminal complaint says, Peters ordered Mendoza an Uber to his family’s residence in Chatham, Massachusetts, a seaside town at the southeastern tip of Cape Cod.

Mendoza said Peters’ mother and grandmother greeted her when she arrived at the house on May 23, 2025, early in the evening, according to the criminal complaint. She then went into Peters’ bedroom, where they livestreamed on Twitch while drinking alcohol. According to the criminal complaint, Mendoza told police she felt “peer-pressured” to drink.

She said Peters “instructed her to say that the alcohol is water, so that neither his Twitch

account nor live stream gets banned,” according to the criminal complaint. After making out on Peters’ couch, Mendoza said she fell asleep in Peters’ bed, according to the criminal complaint.

Mendoza told police that she woke up the next morning to Peters having sex with her, according to the criminal complaint.

“She stated that because it was already occurring, she did not tell Mr. Peters to stop,” the criminal complaint says. “Ms. Mendoza advised that she did not consent to the sexual intercourse.”

Mendoza told police she did not say anything to Peters as he was on top of her because she was in “shock,” and that she never verbally consented to the sex. She said that after Peters finished having sex with her “he was so cold” and ordered her an Uber home, according to the criminal complaint.

In her civil lawsuit, Mendoza additionally alleged Peters had sex with her when she was drunk “to the point where she was unable to give consent.” The criminal complaint did not mention that allegation.

Mendoza did not receive a sexual assault forensic exam after the encounter, according to the criminal complaint.

According to the criminal complaint, she initially told police she told a friend about the encounter but could not provide the friend’s contact information at the time. When police called her back later, she told them she “did not tell anyone the full extent of what occurred,” according to the criminal complaint.

Police attempted to contact Peters multiple times in response to the allegations, per the criminal complaint, but he did not contact authorities as of Aug. 30.

Mendoza said she saw Peters again in November 2025 after they ran into each other at a networking event in Miami, her civil lawsuit says. Peters then allegedly invited Mendoza and her friends to his place in Delray Beach, Florida, for a streaming session on Kick.

Mendoza alleged that during the livestream, Peters injected her with a syringe of Aqualyx, a fat-dissolving compound he did not reveal was not approved by the Food and Drug Administration, which he said would reduce fat in her face, without her consent, according to the civil lawsuit.

“The video shows that Peters had problems injecting Mendoza. In fact, Mendoza’s right cheek has perforated,” the civil lawsuit says, adding that Peters allegedly suggested that the syringe contained methamphetamine.

Peters and Mendoza saw each other a handful of times after that, including instances where Peters paid bouncers to let Mendoza into bars and purchased alcoholic drinks for her, according to the civil lawsuit.

In July, Peters filed a motion to dismiss several counts and challenged the sexual misconduct claim, which was added in an amended complaint. That motion is still pending. Peters is set to be deposed on Oct. 1, and the case remains pending.

Over the last few years, Peters has gained enormous fame as something of a godfather of “looksmaxxing,” an online phenomenon among young men. “Looksmaxxing” is the general practice of trying to maximize your physical appearance through a wide range of dieting, exercise and grooming habits. It promotes men with sharp jawlines, low body fat and symmetrical faces.

“Looksmaxxers” sometimes attempt to achieve the optimal male physique through extreme measures, including “bone smashing,” or using a hammer to intentionally break facial bones so they grow back more defined. Experts have called the trend potentially unhealthy and dangerous.

The new charges against Peters are not his first run-in with the law.

Peters and two other people were charged in April in Florida with shooting at an alligator. He and another person pleaded no contest to unlawfully discharging a firearm in public and were given six months of probation and ordered to serve 20 hours of community service, according to NBC South Florida.

He was also hospitalized in April in Miami after a suspected overdose, according to his representative. He said in a livestream at the time, after being released from the hospital, that “I ain’t gonna be doing any more substances for a little while, hopefully for forever.”

World.title: Hayden Panettiere died from accidental overdose of drugs, including fentanyl, coroner says
World.content:
“Heroes” and “Nashville” star Hayden Panettiere’s death has been ruled an accident caused by the toxic effects of multiple drugs, including fentanyl, officials said Tuesday.

The Greenville County Coroner’s Office attributed her cause of death to the toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine.

There were no signs of trauma that would have contributed to the death, the release added.

Panettiere, 36, died Aug. 16 at a South Carolina apartment complex where she had been staying. Authorities found her unresponsive after a report of a cardiac arrest.

The Greenville Police Department said there were no signs of foul play during the initial response and investigation. The investigation into her death remains active, the department said Tuesday.

The Drug Enforcement Administration was also investigating Panettiere’s death.

Bill Bodner, the former special agent in charge of the DEA’s Los Angeles Field Division, noted that the quantity of drugs found in Panettiere’s system remains unclear. But three of the drugs listed in her autopsy became common among drug abusers in the 1990s and remain widely used.

The cocktail’s street name, he said, is “the Holy Trinity.”

Bodner identified those drugs as an opiate, which in Panettiere’s case was fentanyl; a muscle relaxer, or Methocarbamol; and an anti-anxiety medication, or Alprazolam.

Quetiapine is an antipsychotic drug typically used to treat conditions such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and major depressive disorder. 4-ANPP, or 4-Anilinopiperidine, is a precursor chemical used in the illicit manufacture of fentanyl, Bodner said.

He described the precursor as a likely sign that the fentanyl found in her system was illegal. The drug cocktail, he added, is “incredibly dangerous.”

“When used in combination, there’s a synergism,” he said.

Panettiere’s on-again, off-again boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, was at the apartment complex at the time of her death and showed authorities what a police report described as a “bag of medication” he said she was taking.

An attorney for Hickerson did not immediately respond Tuesday to a request for comment on Panettiere’s death. Panettiere’s mother, Lesley Vogel, also did not immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday.

Bodner, who probed the overdose deaths of Michael Jackson, Matthew Perry and other celebrities, has said investigators were likely attempting to reconstruct Panettiere’s final days.

“They will use forensics to exploit her telephone, try to re-create the last two or three days of her life from looking at text messages, looking at phone calls, looking at interaction with people on social media,” the 32-year veteran of the DEA’s field office in Los Angeles said.

“Once there’s a timeline of what she was doing before her death, it becomes easier to kind of find where that drug distribution took place that killed her,” Bodner added.

Panettiere’s relationship with Hickerson — an aspiring actor from South Carolina — appeared to have ended in 2020 amid allegations of domestic violence, but her mother told NBC News that they were still seeing each other when she died.

Panettiere detailed those allegations, along with her struggles with addiction and postpartum depression, in her recently released memoir, “This Is Me: A Reckoning.”

Hickerson pleaded no contest to a charge of injuring a spouse or girlfriend in 2019 in Los Angeles, and he was sentenced to four years of probation, court records show. Panettiere sought a restraining order against Hickerson in 2020, though the outcome is unclear.

In a statement in August, a lawyer for Hickerson reiterated that police found no signs of foul play in Panettiere’s death. The attorney, Sloan Ellis, added that the actor’s death remained under investigation.

“Out of respect for Hayden’s loved ones and the ongoing investigation, there will be no further comment at this time,” Ellis said at the time.

Panettiere began appearing in television commercials as a child. She landed a breakout role on the NBC sci-fi series “Heroes” and later earned two Golden Globe nominations for portraying an ambitious and volatile country musician in “Nashville.”

In her memoir, Panettiere wrote that her life began to spiral after she had a daughter with Ukrainian heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko in 2014. She began drinking heavily to cope with postpartum depression and Klitschko’s distance, she wrote.

Panettiere checked into rehab and gave Klitschko custody of their child in 2018.

If you or someone you know is struggling with a drug or substance abuse problem, call these numbers for help: The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration’s national helpline is 1-800-662-HELP (1-800-662-4357); the National Drug Helpline is 1-844-289-0879; and the American Addiction Centers’ hotline is (866) 464-3073.

World.title: Simone Biles says three masked men burglarized her home and stole her car
World.content:
Olympic gold medalist Simone Biles is down one luxury car and up one security dog after three masked men stole her Porsche GTS, she told her TikTok followers on Monday.

“Get ready with me to pick up my new car,” the gymnast said with an upbeat squeal as she applied makeup in her bathroom.

Biles, 29, said the robbery happened during her last months in Chicago and is partially responsible for why she and her husband, Jonathan Owens, now have a Dobermann Pinscher.

“I feel like I need a reality TV show,” Biles said. “The things that happen to me are absolute insanity.”

Gymnast Simone Biles before the game between the Chicago Bears and the Los Angeles Rams at Soldier Field on Sept. 29, 2024 in Chicago. Michael Reaves / Getty Images file

Chicago police said it could not provide an incident report to NBC News.

In recent years, several high-profile athletes across multiple sports have reported home break-ins and robberies.

Kansas City Chiefs players Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce were both robbed in October 2024. The homes of basketball pros Sabrina Ionescu of the New York Liberty and Karl-Anthony Towns of the New York Knicks were robbed in 2025. The home of Shedeur Sanders of the Cleveland Browns was robbed by four men as he played a game earlier this year.

Biles said her old car was recovered but she and Owens, a safety for the Indianapolis Colts, decided to get a new one anyway: “When they turned that thing on, I was sold,” she said.

The world’s most decorated gymnast made headlines in June when she revealed on social media that she almost died, though she did not share the circumstances.

“I’m not one to normally share things like this because I value privacy in today’s age,” Biles said in a post, “but almost dying wasn’t on my bingo card earlier this week.”

World.title: Grand jury declines to indict anyone in death of Nolan Wells
World.content:
The grand jury reviewing the case of Nolan Wells, an 18-year-old who was found dead after going missing following an outing with friends on Mississippi's Horn Island on the Fourth of July, has determined there was no criminal wrongdoing in the teen's death.

Wells' death sparked a considerable amount of speculation across social media, much of which was rebuked by the grand jury.

"The Grand Jury finds no credible evidence to support the public allegations that any persons who rode to or from Horn Island on July 4, 2026, on the Triton, the Palm Beach, or the Tideline engaged in any criminal conduct related to the death of Mr. Wells," the report states. "The allegations against the occupants of the Triton, the Palm Beach, and the Tideline [boats that traveled to the island] are not based in truth, and are solely the result of public clamor and private malice."

"In addition to bringing prosecutions against the guilty, the grand jury must also exonerate those who have been falsely accused," Jackson County District Attorney Angel Myers McIlrath said in a video statement.

"There is absolutely no evidence to support the allegations that Nolan's disappearance and death were racially motivated," she said. "Nolan's friends loved Nolan, and Nolan loved them."

A person holds a picture of Nolan Xavier Wells during a news conference at National Action Network headquarters, July 10, 2026, in New York. Yuki Iwamura/AP

Wells had traveled to Horn Island with his friends to celebrate the Fourth of July, but didn't return to the mainland with them that afternoon, Jackson County Sheriff John Ledbetter said at the time.

He was last seen on the island at 3 p.m., according to the office of civil rights attorney Ben Crump, who is representing the family. Wells' mother reported him missing later that night. His body was found Monday, July 6, off the coast of the island, which is about 10 miles south of the Mississippi mainland.

According to the report, the grand jury concluded the "position of, condition of, time of discovery, and location of Mr. Wells' body is consistent with drowning."

An independent autopsy commissioned by the family could not determine Wells' cause of death, Crump said in late July. The results of that independent autopsy, released by the family on Tuesday, found that Wells suffered blunt force injuries to the back of his head and to his body. The autopsy determined that although alcohol was found in his system, the exact amount could not be determined, nor was it clear when he may have consumed the alcohol or what his blood-alcohol level was.

"There still remains gaps in information that would define the condition of Nolan Wells (i.e. conscious or unconscious, forced or unforced) before entering or while in the water that would lead to drowning," independent forensic pathologist Dr. Roger Mitchell Jr. wrote in his report. "This forensic pathologist is not convinced based upon the review of the investigative witness summaries or the post-mortem toxicology that Nolan Wells was too intoxicated to swim."

The results of the autopsy conducted by the Mississippi State Medical Examiner have not been publicly released, but the grand jury said in its report that the state also ruled the cause of death as "undetermined."

The grand jury stated that both Mitchell's autopsy and the state's found that Wells had bruising on the back of his head. However, it said the two autopsies disagreed about the "presence of bruising (non-deep tissue) on Mr. Wells' buttocks and shoulder."

The grand jury also noted that it could not definitively state what caused any of those injuries.

"Two medical examiners found contusions on the back of Nolan's head, and Dr. Roger Mitchell found bruises on his back," Crump said in a news conference alongside the family Tuesday. "What caused them and did they contribute to his death? We'll never know, they say."

Wells' friends have told authorities that he chose to stay behind on the island to speak with a girl, telling them he would come back to the mainland later.

Wells' parents, Christine and Elmore Wonsley, previously told "CBS Mornings" they didn't believe their son would have stayed behind by choice.

"No, he wouldn't. Nolan always stays with the group," Elmore Wonsley, Nolan's father, told "CBS Mornings." "If you be with me, you come back with me. So that I don't understand, and with me being a parent, if I was in that situation, I would have told them, 'You're going to get back on this boat with me because I don't want to answer to your parents if something happens to you.'"

Crump, who is representing the family, told "CBS Mornings," "There are so many glaring contradictions, that's why so many people all across America are chiming in, saying this is not adding up. I mean, you have [his friends] say he was talking to a young lady, and she said that he said, 'I'm going to get back on the boat with the boys.' The boys say, 'He said that, 'No, I'm going to stay with her.' I mean, which is it?"

In a statement released Monday evening, Crump called on the district attorney to keep the investigation into Wells' death open and active.

"We don't know how Nolan died, and neither does the State of Mississippi. Mississippi must keep investigating, and if it will not pursue this to the end, the Department of Justice should," Crump said. "This grand jury result leaves us with more questions than answers. Nolan's family will not rest until we know what happened to him, and neither will we."

The grand jury, which consisted of 23 people who represented a "cross section of citizens" from Jackson County, said in its report released Monday: "the individuals who traveled to or from Horn Island on the Triton, the Palm Beach, and Tideline cooperated fully with this investigation, including offering marine GPS devices, surveillance footage, cell phones, and statements to law enforcement officers and Mr. Wells' family during this investigation."

It also concluded that Wells "chose to remain on Horn Island after the boat he arrived on departed, which is common for visitors to Horn Island on holidays and other crowded days."
